claims: 1. A fiber array adapter, characterized by comprising an adapter input (1 a) and an adapter output (1 b); the input end (1 a) of the adapter is precisely arranged and fixed by the input ends of a plurality of optical fibers to form a two-dimensional array for synchronously receiving multiple paths of independent optical signals, and the input ends of the optical fibers are arranged to be frosted end surfaces; The output ends (1 b) of the adapter are rearranged and fixed by the output ends of the optical fibers to form a one-dimensional linear array for outputting linear optical signals; The optical transmission channels formed by the optical fibers are configured to independently transmit the optical signals received by each point on the two-dimensional array to the corresponding point of the one-dimensional linear array, so that the spatially distributed multi-channel optical signals are converted into linear optical signals.

2. An array channel-based spectroscopic measurement device comprising a spectroscopic analysis module (4) and a fibre-optic array adapter according to claim 1; The spectrum analysis module (4) comprises an incident slit, a dispersion element and an imaging detector which are sequentially arranged along an optical path; the entrance slit is optically coupled to a one-dimensional linear array of the adapter outputs (1 b); the dispersive element splits the optical signal from each fiber channel in the one-dimensional linear array and directs it to a different spatial location of the imaging detector.

3. An array channel based spectroscopic measurement device according to claim 2, further comprising a front-end optical lens (2) detachably arranged at the front end of the fiber array adapter; The front optical lens (2) is optically coupled with the adapter input end (1 a) and is used for converging specific optical information of an object to be detected on the same focal plane.

4. A spectral measurement device based on an array channel according to claim 3, characterized in that the front optical lens (2) is an imaging lens configured to image light rays from different spatial positions of the object to be measured onto different points of the two-dimensional array of adapter inputs (1 a) for realizing a multi-point spectral measurement on a two-dimensional plane.

5. A spectral measurement device based on an array channel according to claim 3, characterized in that the front optical lens (2) is a cone optical lens configured to focus light rays of different angles from the same area of the object to be measured onto different points of the two-dimensional array of the adapter input (1 a) for angular resolved spectral measurement.

6. A spectral measurement device based on an array channel according to claim 3, characterized in that the front optical lens (2) is a near-eye display optical lens configured to image light from a specific optical area of the object to be measured onto different spots of the two-dimensional array of adapter inputs (1 a) for realizing specific optical area measurements.

7. A spectral measurement device based on array channels according to claim 3, further comprising an angle homogenizing structure arranged between the adapter input end (1 a) of the fiber array adapter and the front optical lens (2) for angle homogenizing light rays with different incidence angles from the front optical lens (2) and projecting the light rays to the input end of the optical fiber.

8. The spectral measurement device based on array channels according to claim 7, wherein the angle homogenizing structure is a micro lens array, and the optical axis of each micro lens (7) in the micro lens array is aligned with the optical axis of each optical fiber input end in the two-dimensional array of the adapter input end (1 a) one by one.

9. An array channel-based spectroscopic measurement device according to claim 8, wherein the radius of curvature of each microlens (7) in the microlens array is configured to converge incident light within a predetermined angular range onto the receiving end face of the corresponding optical fiber, and to make the range of incident angles of the light rays ultimately entering the optical fiber smaller than the numerical aperture angle of the optical fiber.

10. An array channel based spectral measurement device according to claim 7, characterized in that the angle homogenizing structure is a diffusion film (8), the diffusion film (8) being configured for homogenizing the spatial angular distribution of the incident light, such that the light exiting through the diffusion film (8) is uniformly incident to the input end of the optical fiber.
11. The array channel-based spectroscopic measurement device of claim 7, wherein the angle-homogenizing structure comprises a switchable microlens array module and a diffusion film module.

records.abstract: The present invention discloses a battery connection module, a battery connection assembly, and a battery connection system. A battery connection module (figure 1, 100), comprises a busbar 2, used for electrical connection to a battery cell; and a connector (figure 3, 1) installed on the busbar 2 for electrically connecting the busbar 2 to a wire 40 of a ribbon cable (figure 2, 4), wherein the connector (figure 3, 1) comprises: a first housing (figure 4, 10); and a first terminal 13 which is set in the first housing (figure 4, 10), wherein the bottom of the first terminal 13 is exposed from the bottom of the first housing (figure 4, 10) and welded to the busbar 2, wherein the first terminal 13 has a wire clamping structure 130, which is used to clamp the wire 40 for electrical connection with the wire 40. [Figure 5]
records.summary: The disclosure describes a battery connection module for electrically linking battery cells to a ribbon-cable wire. The module comprises a busbar for connection to a battery cell and a connector mounted on the busbar. The connector has a first housing and a first terminal set in the housing, with the terminal bottom exposed from the housing bottom and welded to the busbar. The first terminal includes a wire clamping structure that clamps the wire to make electrical connection. records.abstract: CHX Metal (Shenzhen Changhexin Precision Hardware) produces liquid cooling connectors for data center cooling and EV battery thermal management, with dimensional tolerance ±0.005mm and 100% leak testing. ... They connect cooling loops in data centers, EV battery thermal management, energy storage and industrial power electronics.
records.summary: This is a manufacturer product page from CHX Metal (Shenzhen Changhexin Precision Hardware), a precision CNC machining company founded in 2013, describing its liquid cooling connector offerings. The page states that the company machines quick-disconnect couplings, threaded coolant fittings, cold plate connectors, manifold connectors, and blind-mate connectors for server racks, targeting data center cooling, EV battery thermal management, energy storage, and industrial power electronics. It reports a standard dimensional tolerance of ±0.005mm on sealing surfaces, 100% pressure-decay leak testing, and materials including aluminum 6061, stainless steel SUS316, and brass C3604 with O-ring sealing. The content is company self-description and marketing material, not peer-reviewed testing or third-party validation, so the stated tolerances, testing, and quality claims are as-claimed by the manufacturer.

records.abstract: The invention discloses a multi-photon optical fiber array endoscopic imaging device and method based on hollow spiral scanning, and belongs to the technical field of biological imaging. The device comprises a laser collimation beam expansion module, a pulse chirp module, a beam switching module, an endoscopic detection module and a fluorescence acquisition module. The inner detection module drives the optical fiber array to execute hollow spiral scanning through the resonance driver, and the track starting point is not positioned at the view field origin, so that central dense sampling is avoided. The method comprises the steps of switching optical fibers through an optical switch, enabling each optical fiber to execute hollow spiral scanning with misaligned space, collecting multi-photon signals such as fluorescence, second harmonic, fluorescence service life and the like, and obtaining a complete field imaging result through image reconstruction and fusion to complement a central cavity. The invention obviously reduces the photodamage of the central area, improves the uniformity of imaging resolution, ensures reality and reliability based on physical sampling of the fused image, and has high system stability.

claims: 1. A multiphoton fiber optic array endoscopic imaging device based on hollow spiral scanning, characterized in that it comprises: The laser collimation and beam expansion module is used to collimate and expand the femtosecond pulse laser emitted from the laser. The pulse chirp module, connected to the laser collimation and beam expander module, is used to pre-compensate for pulse broadening after optical pulse transmission via optical fiber; The beam switching module, connected to the pulse chirp module, includes an optical switch and an optical fiber array. The optical fiber array includes at least two low group velocity dispersion single-mode fibers. The optical switch is used to selectively couple the laser after pulse chirp compensation to the target fiber in the optical fiber array. The endoscopic detection module, connected to the beam switching module, includes a resonant driver, a package housing, and a micro-objective. The resonant driver is used to drive one end of the fiber array to generate scanning motion. The package housing seals the end of the fiber array, the resonant driver, and the micro-objective. The micro-objective is used to focus the excitation light onto the sample and couple the multiphoton signal of the sample to the fiber array. The fluorescence acquisition module, connected to the beam switching module and the endoscopic detection module, is used to acquire multiphoton signals transmitted by the fiber optic array, perform image reconstruction and fusion processing, and obtain imaging results with a complete field of view. Among them, the resonant driver drives the fiber array to execute a hollow spiral scanning trajectory, and the starting point of the hollow spiral scanning trajectory is not located at the origin of the scanning field of view; The pulse chirp module includes a beam splitter, a prism pair, and a reflector. The prism pair consists of a first prism and a second prism, which are used in conjunction with the reflector to compress the laser pulse to compensate for the broadening of the optical pulse during transmission through the optical fiber. The fluorescence acquisition module includes a dichroic mirror, a bandpass filter group, a lens group, a photomultiplier tube group, a time-correlated single-photon counter, and a computer. The dichroic mirror includes dichroic mirror one and dichroic mirror two, used to separate fluorescence signals and second harmonic signals, respectively. The bandpass filter group includes bandpass filter one and bandpass filter two, used to filter signals in specific wavelength bands, respectively. The lens group includes a third lens and a fourth lens, used to focus signals, respectively. The photomultiplier tube group includes a first photomultiplier tube and a second photomultiplier tube, used to acquire fluorescence signals and second harmonic signals, respectively. The time-correlated single-photon counter is used to acquire fluorescence lifetime signals. The computer is used to control image reconstruction and fusion processing. Among them, the third reflector is set in the optical path of the second harmonic signal and is used to refract the second harmonic signal to the second bandpass filter and the fourth lens.

Provide an optical fiber array, which includes at least two low group velocity dispersive single-mode fibers, and one end of the optical fiber array is driven by a resonant driver. S2. Control the laser to emit femtosecond pulse laser, which, after collimation, beam expansion, and pulse chirp compensation, is selectively coupled to the target fiber in the fiber array through the beam switching module; S3. Switch the beam switching module to other optical fibers in the fiber array, and repeat steps S2-S4 to make the other optical fibers perform hollow spiral scanning trajectories that do not overlap with the target optical fiber space. S6. Reconstruct images from the multiphoton signals collected by each optical fiber to obtain multiple sub-images; S7. Perform fusion processing on multiple sub-images to fill in the central hole region of each hollow spiral scanning trajectory and obtain the imaging result of the complete field of view.

6. The multiphoton fiber optic endoscopic imaging method based on hollow spiral scanning according to claim 5, characterized in that: in step S3, the function of the hollow spiral scanning trajectory is: ; in, It is the radius from the current point to the origin. It's the angle. The initial radius and , The radial growth factor is the initial radius. The value ranges from 0.1 mm to 2 mm.

7. The multiphoton fiber array endoscopic imaging method based on hollow spiral scanning according to claim 5, characterized in that: in step S4, the multiphoton signal further includes a fluorescence lifetime signal, the fluorescence lifetime signal is acquired by a time-correlated single-photon counter, and the laser provides a synchronization signal for the acquisition of the fluorescence lifetime signal.

records.abstract: A novel copper-aluminum composite terminal, including a connecting part and a functional part which are connected to each other, the functional part is made of an aluminum-clad copper composite material which comprises an inner copper layer and an outer aluminum layer encapsulating the copper layer, the connecting part is connected to a conductive portion of the aluminum cable, and at least part of the copper layer of the functional part is connected to the electric device. The design of this structure enables weight reduction and cost savings.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a copper-aluminum composite terminal for electrically connecting an aluminum cable to an electric device. The terminal has a connecting part joined to the aluminum cable's conductive portion and a functional part made of an aluminum-clad copper composite material, with an inner copper layer encapsulated by an outer aluminum layer; at least part of the copper layer connects to the electric device. The stated aim is weight reduction and cost savings from this structure. The available text covers the abstract and all 19 claims only; the description and figures were not retrieved, and no experimental performance data are supplied.
records.why_it_matters: It proposes a terminal architecture that places copper only where device contact occurs while using aluminum for cable-side connection, potentially reducing copper content and mass in aluminum-cable terminations.

records.abstract: Translated from Korean 패키지는 브리징 요소(OMIB)와 제1 및 제2 광자 경로를 포함하여, 양방향 광자 경로를 형성한다. OMIB는 하나 이상의 다이와 연결되기 위한 제1 및 제2 상호 연결 영역을 갖는다. 제3 및 제4 단방향 광자 경로는 제1 상호 연결 영역과 광 인터페이스(OI) 사이를 결합할 수 있다. 광자 트랜시버는 OMIB에서의 제1 부분, 및 다이 중 하나에서의 제2 부분을 갖는다. 제1 및 제2 부분은 길이가 2㎜ 미만인 전기 상호 연결부를 통해 결합될 수 있다. 다이는 제2 부분에 인접한 중앙 영역 주위에 있는 컴퓨팅 요소를 포함한다. OMIB는 게르마늄, 실리콘, 게르마늄의 합금, 실리콘의 합금, 인듐 인화물(InP)을 기반으로 하는 III-V족 재료 또는 갈륨 비소화물(GaAs)을 기반으로 하는 III-V족 재료로 제작된 전기 흡수 변조기를 포함할 수 있다. OMIB는 변조기에 대한 온도 보상을 포함할 수 있다. The package includes an OMIB and first and second photonic paths, forming a bidirectional photonic path. The OMIB has first and second interconnect regions for connecting to one or more dies. Third and fourth unidirectional photonic paths can couple between the first interconnect region and an optical interface (OI). The photonic transceiver has a first portion in the OMIB and a second portion in one of the dies. The first and second portions can be coupled via electrical interconnects less than 2 mm in length. The dies include computing elements around a central region adjacent to the second portion. The OMIB can include an electroabsorbing modulator fabricated from germanium, silicon, an alloy of germanium, an alloy of silicon, a group III-V material based on indium phosphide (InP), or a group III-V material based on gallium arsenide (GaAs). The OMIB can include temperature compensation for the modulator.
records.summary: The disclosure describes an optical multi-die interconnect bridge (OMIB) that optically and electrically couples two dies. The bridge contains a photonic network with waveguides, a modulator, a photodetector, and an edge coupler providing an optical interface to fibers, plus analog/mixed-signal (AMS) blocks with serializer/deserializer circuits that connect to each die via an electrical interface supporting a communication protocol. A photonic channel forms a data path from serializer through modulator, photonic path, photodetector, and parallelizer between the joined dies. The abstract further describes a photonic transceiver split between the OMIB and a die, coupled by electrical interconnects under 2 mm, with computing elements arranged around a central die region, and modulators fabricated from germanium, silicon, Ge/Si alloys, InP-based III-V, or GaAs-based III-V materials, optionally with temperature compensation. No measured performance data are supplied; the text is abstract and claims only.
records.why_it_matters: It suggests an architecture for chiplet-to-chiplet links that places the optical transceiver partly in a silicon bridge and partly in the die, keeping the electrical interface short (under 2 mm) while using WDM photonics for the longer reach.

records.title: High-power shielded busbars for electric vehicle charging and power distribution
records.abstract: Translated from Korean A unitary busbar transmits power from one connection point to another in an electric vehicle. A unitary busbar comprises a central solid-core conductor, an insulating layer over the solid-core conductor, and an electromagnetic shield fitted around the insulation. The unitary busbar can be bent into specific configurations to fit the electric vehicle body.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a unitary busbar for electric-vehicle power distribution that combines a solid-core conductor, an insulating layer, and a conductive shielding layer compressed against the insulation, with at least one connector formed from the solid core itself. The busbar is described as bendable to follow the vehicle's internal configuration and is grounded to the vehicle through a rigid ground conductor connected to the shielding layer. The claims describe a system in which the busbar links a first connection point, such as a charging port, to a second connection point, such as a battery connector. Dependent claims recite materials and dimensions, including aluminum or copper conductors and shields, XLPE/PVC/silicone insulation, conductor cross-sections of 3–300 mm², insulation thickness of 0.9–1.1 mm, and shield thickness of 0.5–2 mm. One dependent claim states the busbar can support 350 kW charging at 400 V while keeping the shielding layer at or below 120 °C; this is a claim feature, not a demonstrated experimental result in the supplied text.
records.why_it_matters: The disclosure describes integrating shielding and grounding into a single bendable busbar, which could simplify routing and EMI containment in high-power EV charging and distribution architectures.

records.title: Demountable coupling of optical connector and optoelectronic device
assignees: 美商扇港元器件有限公司
records.abstract: Optical alignment of a receptacle at an aligned position on an optoelectronic device body is accomplished using an alignment optical connector that is demountably attached to the receptacle by matching passive alignment features on the facing surfaces between the receptacle and the alignment optical connector. The device body includes a first row of at least two data optical ports, and a second row of alignment input and output ports parallel to and spaced from the first row of data optical ports by a parallel spacing. The data optical ports communicate with the optoelectronic device. The alignment ports correspond to a loopback waveguide. The aligned position of the receptacle is determined from the loopback waveguide. The receptacle is permanently attached to the device body at this aligned position. A data optical connector is similarly configured as the alignment optical connector, in the manner in which optical fibers are supported to input/output optical signals and with similar passive alignment features, but the passive alignment features are referenced to the optical fibers by an offset equivalent to the parallel spacing between the first and second rows. The second row is same or shorter than the first row. The number of data optical ports is greater or equal to the number of alignment optical ports. The data optical ports and the alignment optical ports are arranged in a 2 x N matrix.
records.summary: The disclosure describes an optoelectronic device body with a first column of at least two active data optical ports (e.g., grating couplers) and a second, parallel column of alignment input/output ports spaced from the data ports by a defined parallel spacing. The alignment ports correspond to a loopback/feedback waveguide, so an alignment optical connector with matching passive alignment features can be demountably attached and used to actively determine the correct alignment position of a receptacle on the device body. Once aligned, the receptacle is permanently attached to the device body, and the alignment connector is removed. A data optical connector is configured similarly but with its passive alignment features referenced to its fibers by an offset equal to the parallel spacing between the two rows, enabling passively aligned detachable coupling of data fibers. The abstract states the ports are arranged in a 2 x N matrix, with the second row same or shorter than the first and data ports numbering at least as many as alignment ports. No measured performance data are supplied; the text is limited to abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: It separates the one-time active alignment of a permanently fixed receptacle from routine connector mating, so subsequent data connectors can be attached and detached using only passive alignment features referenced by a fixed offset.

records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricant composition built around an ionic liquid whose cation is a quaternary structure of general formula (B), with R5, R6 and R7 each independently a linear or branched alkyl group of 1 to 22 carbon atoms and R8 either a linear or branched alkyl group of 1 to 22 carbon atoms or a hydroxyalkyl group —CnH2n—OH with n from 1 to 22, paired with an anion of general formula (C) in which R9 and R10 are each independently linear or branched alkyl groups of 1 to 10 carbon atoms. The independent claim covers this ionic-liquid-containing lubricant composition; dependent claims add a base oil and specify that the base oil is at least one of a poly-α-olefin and a polyol ester. The available text is a search snippet with claims only, so no measured friction, wear, thermal-stability or viscosity data are reported here. The filing is assigned to Minebea Mitsumi and carries publication number JP7757242B2.

records.title: Fiber array launcher assembly
records.abstract: A fiber array launcher assembly including a hollow body having a front end and a rear end; an alignment plate having an array of holes coupled to the rear end of the body; a beam shaper having an array of lenses coupled to the front end of the body, where a separate lens is aligned with each hole in the alignment plate; and a plurality of fiber assemblies each including a fiber having an end face spliced to an end of an endcap where the endcap has a larger diameter than a diameter of the fiber, and where a separate endcap is secured in each hole so that the fiber is aligned with the associated lens.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a fiber array launcher assembly that aligns multiple fibers to a corresponding array of lenses. A hollow body carries an alignment plate with an array of holes at its rear end and a beam shaper with an array of lenses at its front end, with one lens aligned to each hole. Each fiber assembly has a fiber end face spliced to an endcap of larger diameter than the fiber, and each endcap is secured in a hole so the fiber aligns with its associated lens and extends into the hollow body. The disclosure also describes a method of positioning each endcap in a hole, aligning the fiber to a micro-lens, gluing the endcap with a curable glue, and repeating until all holes are populated. No measured optical performance or experimental results are provided in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The spliced larger-diameter endcap seated in a matching alignment-plate hole provides a mechanical registration feature that may simplify passive alignment of each fiber to its lens, and the glued mounting is described as allowing re-alignment or replacement by heating the glue.

records.title: New copper-aluminum composite terminal
assignees: Changchun Jetty Automotive Technology Co., Ltd.
records.abstract: A novel copper-aluminum composite terminal, including a connecting part and a functional part which are connected to each other, the functional part is made of an aluminum-clad copper composite material which comprises an inner copper layer and an outer aluminum layer encapsulating the copper layer, the connecting part is connected to a conductive portion of the aluminum cable, and at least part of the copper layer of the functional part is connected to the electric device. The design of this structure enables weight reduction and cost savings.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a copper-aluminum composite terminal for electrically connecting an aluminum cable to an electric device. The terminal has a connecting part joined to the aluminum cable's conductive portion and a functional part made of an aluminum-clad copper composite material, with an inner copper layer encapsulated by an outer aluminum layer; at least part of the copper layer of the functional part connects to the electric device. The abstract states that this structure enables weight reduction and cost savings, but no measured values or test data are supplied. The available text covers the abstract and 19 claims only; the description and figures were not retrieved, and the English view may be machine translated.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed architecture places aluminum at the cable-side connection and copper at the device-side contact within one terminal, which is intended to address the weight and cost of an all-copper terminal while retaining a copper interface at the functional end.

records.title: Liquid cooling high-density pluggable modules for a network element
records.abstract: A network element include one or more modules each supporting one or more pluggable modules; and a first manifold and a second manifold each configured to connect to a conduit associated with a coldplate, wherein one of the first manifold and the second manifold is an inlet manifold and the other is an outlet manifold for a cooling fluid that flows through the conduit to cool the one or more pluggable modules. The one or more pluggable modules can be each a pluggable optical module that is one of compliant to any of XFP, SFP, XENPAK, X2, CFP, CFP2, CFP4, CFP8, QSFP, QSFP+, QSFP28, OSFP, and QSFP-DD and have a housing that has dimensions similar to any of XFP, SFP, XENPAK, X2, CFP, CFP2, CFP4, CFP8, QSFP, QSFP+, QSFP28, OSFP, and QSFP-DD.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a pluggable optical module whose main body integrates a coldplate formed from a plate and a lid, with a conduit of one or more channels formed in the plate and enclosed by the lid to contain cooling fluid flow. First and second plug fluid connectors are each in fluid communication with opposite ends of the conduit, allowing the module to connect to external cooling-fluid manifolds. A related network element is described in which such a pluggable module is received within a module, with the network element having first and second manifolds acting as inlet and outlet for cooling fluid. The abstract further states the pluggable modules can be pluggable optical modules compliant with, or having housing dimensions similar to, form factors such as XFP, SFP, XENPAK, X2, CFP, CFP2, CFP4, CFP8, QSFP, QSFP+, QSFP28, OSFP, and QSFP-DD. No measured thermal performance or experimental results are supplied in the available abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: It describes moving liquid cooling into the pluggable module itself via an integrated coldplate and pluggable fluid connectors, rather than relying solely on host-level air or coldplate cooling, which is relevant to thermal management of high-density pluggable optics.

records.abstract: Translated from Chinese 用于测量光的系统和方法，该系统和方法使用共享的收集和放大光学元件，收集并测量从沿着流动池的长度的不同位置发出的光；分光模块，将放大光分成多个波长范围；以及球面透镜阵列，将不同波长和发射位置的光导向探测器阵列。 Systems and methods for measuring light that use shared collection and amplification optics to collect and measure light emitted from different locations along the length of a flow cell; a beam splitter module to separate the amplified light into multiple wavelength ranges; and a spherical lens array to direct light of different wavelengths and emission locations to a detector array.

claims: 1. An optical system for measuring light, the system comprising: a) A flow cell having a length and a width that allow biological cells to pass through; b) A plurality of different excitation light sources that direct light to different locations along the length of the flow cell; c) A shared light collecting optical element and a shared amplifying optical element configured to collect light emitted from different positions of the flow cell and amplify and focus the collected light onto a focal plane of a specified distance according to different wavelength ranges, and amplify and focus the collected light onto different positions along the focal plane according to each different position of the flow cell from which the light is emitted; d) A spectroscopic module comprising spectroscopic optical elements arranged in such a way that they are shared by amplified light emitted from each different location of the flow cell and configured to split amplified light emitted from each different location of the flow cell into an array of channels, each channel corresponding to a separate wavelength range; e) An array of detection modules, wherein each detection module is dedicated to a single channel in the array of channels, each detection module comprising: i) A spherical lens array located at each different focusing distance for each different wavelength range along the propagation direction of the collected light, each spherical lens in the array being configured to receive amplified light emitted from one of the different positions of the flow cell and to direct the received amplified light to a predetermined area on a corresponding photodetector, and Ii) a photodetector array configured to measure the amplified light directed from each spherical lens such that one photodetector measures the collected light in one wavelength range from one of the different locations of the flow cell.
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of excitation light sources comprises a plurality of laser light sources.
3. The system of claim 2, wherein the laser light source is shaped into a designed geometry by beam shaping optics and focused to different locations within the flow cell.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of different excitation light sources comprises more than 5 excitation light sources, optionally more than 10 excitation light sources, optionally more than 15 excitation light sources.
5. The system of claim 1, wherein the distance between adjacent locations on the flow cell to which light is directed from the excitation light source is 25 to 250 μιη, optionally 50 to 150 μιη.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein the shared light collection optics direct light to the shared amplifying optics that amplify a vertical separation distance between light emitted from different locations of the flow cell.

7. The system of claim 6, wherein the shared magnification optical element comprises a set of objective lenses having a magnification of 20 to 250 times, alternatively 30 to 100 times, alternatively 35 to 75 times, alternatively 40 to 60 times.
8. The system of claim 6, wherein the vertical separation distance between adjacent lights is less than 30mm at the spherical lens array.
9. The system of claim 8, wherein the vertical separation distance is 1mm to 10mm at the spherical lens array.

10. The system of claim 9, wherein the plurality of excitation light sources direct light to adjacent locations along the flow cell that are 100 μιη apart, the shared magnifying optical element has a magnification of 55 times, and adjacent light received at the spherical lens array is separated by 5.5mm.

11. The system of claim 1, wherein the light splitting module propagates light through a series of dichroic mirrors and bandpass filters to split amplified light into a plurality of different wavelength ranges.
12. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of wavelength ranges includes a wavelength range from 320nm to 1000 nm.
13. The system of claim 12, wherein the excitation light source comprises lasers of 349nm, 405nm, 488nm, 561nm, and 637 nm.

14. The system of claim 12, wherein the different wavelength ranges include 372nm to 389nm, 417nm to 431nm, 431nm to 449nm, 449nm to 461nm, 461nm to 477nm, 500nm to 517nm, 517nm to 534nm, 534nm to 552nm, 573nm to 592nm, 592nm to 608nm, 608nm to 628nm, 650nm to 672nm, 672nm to 691nm, 691nm to 709nm, 709nm to 726nm, 726nm to 744nm, 744nm to 770nm, 770nm to 798nm, and 798nm to 832nm.

15. The system of claim 1, wherein the light emitted from the different locations oscillates in response to a change in a characteristic of the fluid passing through the flow channel and/or a change in the positioning of the excitation light source.
16. The system of claim 15, wherein the spherical lens of each array directs rocking light to the same area of the photodetector where the detected light is stable.
17. The system of claim 1, wherein the photodetector system comprises a silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) detector.
18. The system of claim 1, wherein each spherical lens is specifically designed such that the diameter of the spot on the photodetector corresponds to the effective detection area of the detector.

19. The system of claim 1, wherein the collection optics and spherical mirror are defined such that detected spots on the respective photodetectors are not affected by positional variations of the collected light focused on the spherical lens.

20. The system of claim 1, wherein the spherical lens is designed to make the detected optical signals on the respective photodetectors insensitive to fluctuations in the horizontal position of biological cells within the flow channel.
21. The system of claim 1, further comprising a set of alignment optics configured to align the amplified light to the spectroscopic module and the spherical lens array.
22. A flow cytometer comprising the system of claim 1.

23. A method for characterizing a biological cell, the method comprising: a) Passing a biological cell through a flow cell, the biological cell being labeled with a plurality of fluorescent labels that fluoresce at different wavelengths when excited, a tag attached to or not present in a cellular component collectively characterizing the biological cell by the presence, absence, or abundance of the labels; b) Directing light to different locations along the length of the flow cell as the biological cells pass through the different locations; c) Collecting light emitted from each of the different locations of the flow cell as the biological cells pass through; d) Amplifying and focusing the collected light to different focusing distances according to different wavelength ranges, and amplifying and focusing the collected light to different positions within each focusing distance according to each different position of the flow cell from which the collected light is emitted; e) Splitting the amplified light into a plurality of different wavelength ranges, wherein different fluorescent wavelengths are divided between the plurality of different wavelength ranges; f) Receiving, by the same array of spherical lenses, light of the same wavelength range emitted from different locations along the length of the flow cell, wherein different spherical lenses within each array receive light emitted from different locations of the flow cell; g) Directing light from each of the spherical lenses to a different photodetector, and H) Measuring light at each of the different photodetectors, thereby identifying the presence, absence or abundance of the marker and identifying a cellular component to characterize the biological cell.

records.abstract: The present invention relates to a lubricating oil composition comprising or produced by mixing of: (A) at least one base oil; (B) at least one dispersant; and (C) at least one detergent, wherein the at least one dispersant includes 2.0 mass% or more of at least one non-borated poly(alkenyl)succinimide ("PIBSA-PAM") based on a total mass of the lubricating oil composition, the polyalkenyl is derived from polyisobutylene, and the imide is derived from a polyamine, the at least one detergent together provides soap in an amount of 0.1 to 0.9 mass% based on the total mass of the lubricating oil composition to the lubricating oil composition, and a ratio of a mass% of the at least one non-borated PIBSA-PAM to a mass% of the soap in the lubricating oil composition is 6.65 or more based on the total mass of the lubricating oil composition.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricating oil composition containing less than 1000 ppm phosphorus, intended to provide valvetrain wear protection in a Ford 6.7L Power Stroke diesel engine test for soot-induced wear and viscosity control. The composition combines at least 50 mass% base oil, one or more dispersants, and one or more detergents. The dispersant system includes 2.0 mass% or more of non-borated polyisobutylene-derived poly(alkenyl)succinimide (PIBSA-PAM) made from a polyamine, while the detergent(s) supply 0.1 to 0.9 mass% soap. A key claimed feature is a mass ratio of non-borated PIBSA-PAM to soap of at least 6.65, with the composition in SAE 20W-X, 15W-X, 10W-X or 5W-X grades. The claims state that rocker arm wear is less than 120 mg in the Ford 6.7L test, but the supplied text contains no experimental data demonstrating this result.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a formulation window linking dispersant-to-soap ratio, low phosphorus content and viscosity grade to a specific engine wear target, giving formulators a compositional lever for soot-related valvetrain wear in low-phosphorus heavy-duty diesel oils.

This is directly relevant to advanced lubricant formulation engineering, but the claims are compositional ranges without disclosed measured data beyond a single claimed wear threshold. The abstract and claims are fully supplied, but the description, examples, and comparative data are absent, so performance and novelty over prior art cannot be verified.

technical_points: Independent claim 1 requires less than 1000 ppm phosphorus, at least 50 mass% base oil, 2.0-6.00 mass% PIBSA-PAM (with at least 2.0 mass% non-borated), 0.1-0.9 mass% soap from detergent(s), a non-borated PIBSA-PAM-to-soap mass ratio of at least 6.65, and an SAE 20W-X/15W-X/10W-X/5W-X grade.
Dependent claims narrow phosphorus to 700-900 ppm, the ratio to 7.0-15.0, and the viscosity grade to 15W-40, 5W-30 or 10W-30.
Detergent embodiments include oil-soluble neutral or overbased calcium and/or magnesium sulfonates and salicylates, with no more than 50 mass% calcium salicylate and optionally no phenate detergent.

PIBSA-PAM embodiments distinguish high molecular weight (polyisobutylene Mn of 1600 g/mol or more by GPC-PS) from low molecular weight (below 1600 g/mol) species, with a high-to-low mass ratio below 3.65 in one dependent claim.
A dependent claim states rocker arm wear of less than 120 mg by the Ford 6.7L Power Stroke Diesel Engine Test for soot-induced wear and viscosity control; the text does not report measured test data.

Optional functionalized polymer embodiments include amine-functionalized hydrogenated isoprene polymers with specified Fv, Fd, Mw/Mn, Mn and Mz values, and the disclosure also covers concentrates and lubrication methods.

records.abstract: Translated from Chinese Lubricant composition providing robust valvetrain wear protection in Ford 6.7L engine test. The present invention relates to a lubricating oil composition containing less than 1000 ppm phosphorus, comprising or admixed with: A) one or more base oils, B) one or more dispersants, wherein the one or more dispersants comprise at least 2.0 mass % of one or more unborated poly(alkenyl) succinimides, wherein the polyalkenyl is derived from polyisobutylene and the imide is derived from a polyamine ("PIBSA-PAM"), based on the total mass of the lubricating oil composition; and C) one or more detergents, wherein the one or more detergents together provide the lubricating oil composition with soap in an amount of 0.1 to 0.9 mass % based on the total mass of the lubricating oil composition; wherein the lubricating oil composition has a ratio of the mass % of the one or more unborated PIBSA-PAM to the soap, based on the total mass of the lubricating oil composition, of 6.65 or more.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a low-phosphorus lubricating oil composition (less than 1000 ppm P) intended to provide valve train wear protection in the Ford 6.7L Power Stroke diesel engine test. The composition combines at least 50 mass % base oil, one or more dispersants including at least 2.0 mass % unboronated polyisobutylene-derived polyamine succinimide (PIBSA-PAM), and one or more detergents supplying 0.1–0.9 mass % soap, with a mass ratio of unboronated PIBSA-PAM to soap of 6.65 or more. The composition is constrained to SAE viscosity grades 20W-X, 15W-X, 10W-X or 5W-X (X = 8, 12, 16, 20, 30 or 40). Dependent claims add features such as 700–900 ppm phosphorus, Group II base oil, sulfonate detergents, low calcium salicylate content, high/low molecular weight PIBSA-PAM splits, and optional functionalized polymers. Claim 24 states the composition provides less than 120 mg valve train rocker arm wear by the Ford 6.7L test, but the supplied text contains no experimental data, so this is a claim feature rather than a demonstrated result.
records.why_it_matters: For formulators targeting low-phosphorus oils, the disclosure frames the unboronated PIBSA-PAM-to-soap mass ratio (≥6.65) as a compositional lever for valve train wear protection, rather than relying solely on phosphorus antiwear chemistry.

Claim 24 and claim 44 tie the formulation to a Ford 6.7L valve train rocker arm wear target (<120 mg), which is directly relevant to the Advanced Lubricants theme. However, the supplied text is abstract and claims only; no examples, comparative data, or measured results are provided, so the wear benefit is asserted rather than demonstrated.

evidence_meta.coverage: All claim text returned by this publication page; English view may be machine translated. Figures and description are not included.

technical_points: Independent claim 1 requires less than 1000 ppm phosphorus, at least 50 mass % base oil, 2.0–6.00 mass % PIBSA-PAM dispersant with at least 2.0 mass % unboronated PIBSA-PAM, and 0.1–0.9 mass % soap from detergents, with an unboronated PIBSA-PAM:soap mass ratio of 6.65 or more.
Claim 1 also limits the composition to SAE grades 20W-X, 15W-X, 10W-X or 5W-X, where X is 8, 12, 16, 20, 30 or 40; claim 20 narrows this to 15W-40, 5W-30 or 10W-30.
Dependent claim 4 specifies 700–900 ppm phosphorus, and claim 5 requires at least 50 mass % of a Group II base oil based on total base oils.

Dependent claims 6–9 favor oil-soluble neutral or overbased calcium and/or magnesium sulfonates, limit calcium salicylate to 50 mass % or less of detergents, and describe compositions substantially free of phenate detergent.

Claims 11–13 describe high molecular weight PIBSA-PAM (PIB Mn ≥1600 g/mol by GPC-PS) and optional low molecular weight PIBSA-PAM, with a high:low mass ratio below 3.65; claim 15 allows 0.05–0.5 mass % boronated PIBSA-PAM.

Claim 24 states less than 120 mg valve train rocker arm wear by the Ford 6.7L Power Stroke Diesel Engine Test for Soot Induced Wear and Viscosity Control; claim 44 optionally ties this threshold to the antiwear method.
Claims 30–41 cover a concentrate with 1 to less than 50 mass % base oil and the same unboronated PIBSA-PAM:soap ratio of 6.65 or more; claims 42–45 cover lubrication methods and a fuel composition.
limitations: Only the abstract and claims were retrieved; the description, examples, and any experimental data are not included, so reported wear performance is not independently evidenced in the supplied text.
The English text may be machine translated from Chinese, so terminology and claim wording should be verified against the original.
No comparative examples, prior-art discussion, or measured test results are available to assess whether the claimed ratio actually delivers the stated wear protection.

records.abstract: An optical path tracing method, applied to an optical cross apparatus comprising a single-row fiber array and a single-row input multidimensional output optical waveguide element, wherein the single-row fiber array is coupled to the single-row input multidimensional output optical waveguide element …
records.summary: The disclosure describes an optical cross-connect apparatus built around a single-row fiber array coupled to a single-row-input, multidimensional-output optical waveguide element. Inside that waveguide element an arbitrarily curved spatial three-dimensional waveguide routes optical signals from single-row input ports to light outlets arranged in a multidimensional pattern. A microlens is formed on the surface of each light outlet by femtosecond laser processing, with no gap between outlet and microlens, and is configured for beam shaping. The disclosure also describes an optical path tracing method using this apparatus and an optical cross device combining the apparatus with a lens system and an optical switching system. Only the abstract and claims were retrieved; the description, figures, and any experimental data are not available, so no measured performance is reported here.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed femtosecond-laser-written, gapless microlens on each waveguide outlet suggests an approach to beam shaping and coupling alignment at the output face of a three-dimensional waveguide fan-out, which is the interface where such cross-connects typically incur loss and alignment sensitivity.

records.abstract: Translated from Spanish The present invention relates to the use of a lubricating composition comprising: - at least one base oil; and - at least one monoester separated from the base oil and formed between a linear, saturated or unsaturated C8-C14 monocarboxylic acid and a branched, saturated or unsaturated C4-C16 monoalcohol, for reducing fuel consumption of a vehicle equipped with a transmission member, in particular a gearbox and/or an axle, lubricated by means of said composition. (Automatic translation with Google Translate, no legal value)
records.summary: The disclosure describes use of a lubricating composition for motor-vehicle transmissions to reduce vehicle fuel consumption. The composition comprises at least one base oil and at least one monoester, distinct from the base oil, formed between a linear C8-C14 monocarboxylic acid and a branched C4-C16 monoalcohol, with the monoester content at or below 30% by weight of the total composition. The transmission element is a gearbox and/or axle lubricated with the composition. The available text is limited to the abstract and claims (English view may be machine translated); no experimental fuel-consumption data, description, or figures were retrieved, so no measured benefit is reported here.
records.why_it_matters: The claims frame a formulation lever for transmission lubricants: a low-viscosity ester (e.g., 2-ethylhexyl dodecanoate) at up to 30 wt% in a Group II/III base-oil blend, which formulators could evaluate as a fuel-economy-oriented alternative to conventional transmission fluids.

records.title: Busbar and battery laminate
assignees: Panasonic Intellectual Property Management Co., Ltd.
records.abstract: A battery module includes: a plurality of batteries stacked together; and a busbar that electrically connects the plurality of batteries with each other. The busbar has: a main body that extends along axis X along which the batteries are stacked together; and a plurality of connectors that protrude from the main body along an axis that intersects with the axis along which the batteries are stacked together, and are electrically connected with terminals of the batteries, respectively. The plurality of batteries are divided into a plurality of battery units. Each of the plurality of battery units includes at least two of the plurality of batteries. The busbar connects the at least two of the plurality of batteries of each of the battery units with each other in parallel. The busbar connects the battery units with each other in series.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a battery module in which multiple batteries are stacked along a first direction and interconnected by a one-piece busbar. The busbar has a main body extending along the stacking direction and connectors protruding along a second direction perpendicular to the stacking direction to contact battery terminals. The batteries are grouped into units of at least two batteries; the busbar connects batteries within each unit in parallel and connects the units to one another in series. The main body's upper surface has a first region and second regions arranged along the stacking direction, with the first region positioned closer to the battery units in a third perpendicular direction and the second regions at both ends of the busbar. The claims also describe dependent features such as connector cross-sections smaller than the main body, differing connector resistances to balance parallel paths, a displacement-allowing portion for relative battery movement, and lower-resistance series sections. No experimental results or measured performance are provided in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed one-piece busbar integrates parallel and series connections in a single stamped or formed part, which may simplify assembly and reduce the number of interconnect components in a stacked battery module.

records.title: Lubricant base oil and lubricant composition
records.abstract: A lubricant base oil for use in the preparation of a cooling lubricant composition, may have a % CP of 60 or more, and the dynamic viscosity at 40° C. is less than 3 mm 2 /s. Such a lubricant base oil may include a base oil (A) having % C p of 60 or more and a kinematic viscosity at 40° C. of less than 3 mm 2 /s, the base oil (A) being 80% by mass or more of the total lubricant base oil mass. Such a lubricant base oil may further include a base oil (B) that is different from the base oil (A), in a range of from 1 to 20% by mass of the total lubricant base oil mass. The base oil (A) may be an isoparaffin-based base oil. Such a lubricant base oil may have a % C N of 21 or less. A cooling lubricant composition may include such a lubricant base oil.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricant base oil intended for preparing a cooling lubricant composition, particularly for cooling electric-vehicle devices. The base oil is defined by a paraffinic carbon fraction (%CP) of 60 or more and a kinematic viscosity at 40°C of less than 3 mm²/s. In embodiments, a base oil (A), optionally an isoparaffin-based base oil, makes up 80% by mass or more of the total base oil, with an optional different base oil (B) at 1–20% by mass, and the base oil may have a %CN of 21 or less. The disclosure also describes cooling lubricant compositions containing this base oil, cooling devices using them, and a method of cooling an electric-vehicle device by circulating the composition. No experimental performance data are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims, so reported benefits are not demonstrated here.
records.why_it_matters: The claims target a low-viscosity, high-paraffinic base oil for direct cooling of EV components such as motors, batteries, inverters, and engines, where low viscosity and thermal/oxidation stability are relevant to heat-transfer and lubrication duties.

records.title: Composition of Lubricant additives
records.abstract: An object of the present invention is to provide a lubricating oil additive composition having an excellent friction reduction effect by forming a tribofilm having increased durability under extreme pressure conditions by including a base oil, a friction improving agent including a borating agent, and an abrasion resistant agent. A lubricating oil additive composition comprising: (a) a base oil; and (b) a friction improver comprising a borating agent is provided.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricating oil additive composition intended to reduce friction by forming a more durable tribofilm under extreme pressure conditions. The composition comprises (a) a base oil and (b) a friction improver containing a boronating agent. Dependent claims specify that the boronating agent may be boric acid, alkyl boron, boric acid ester, or boric acid ester amide, and that the friction improver may include reaction products of a boronating agent with a phosphate ester or phosphate ester amine salt, or with a sulfurized olefin. Certain dependent claims describe the reaction product as a composite amorphous glassy tribofilm of Zn/Fe boron phosphate or Zn/Fe boron sulfide. The claims also recite a friction improver content of 5 to 25 wt% and a kinematic viscosity of 8 to 15 mm²/s at 100°C; no experimental performance data are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed boronating-agent friction improver is directed at forming a durable tribofilm for extreme-pressure lubrication, which is a formulation-level route to friction and wear control in base oils rather than a hardware change.

records.abstract: A lubricating oil composition comprising: a lubricant base oil; (A) a calcium salicylate detergent in an amount of 0.005 to 0.03 mass% in terms of calcium on the basis of the total mass of the composition; (B) a succinimide type ashless dispersant in an amount of 0.005 to 0.25 mass% in terms of …
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricating oil composition intended for lubricating electric motors and transmissions in automobiles. The composition combines a lubricant base oil with tightly limited amounts of (A) a calcium salicylate detergent (0.005–0.03 mass% Ca), (B) a succinimide ashless dispersant (0.005–0.25 mass% N), (C) a nitrogen-containing antioxidant (0.005–0.15 mass% N), and (D) a nitrogen-containing friction modifier at no more than 0.03 mass% N, with total metallic detergent limited to 0.005–0.03 mass% metal. Component (D) includes (D1) a succinimide friction modifier (0.001–0.03 mass% N) made from a C8-36 alkyl/alkenyl succinic acid or anhydride and a polyamine or its N-mono-C1-36 alkyl/alkenyl derivative, while component (B) is a condensation product of a C40-400 alkyl/alkenyl succinic acid or anhydride with a polyamine. Dependent claims add salicylate proportion, phosphite ester, triazole deactivators, viscosity ranges, and an oxidized-oil volume resistivity target; no experimental performance data are supplied in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claim set defines a narrow formulation window in which ash-forming metal, dispersant nitrogen, antioxidant nitrogen, and friction-modifier nitrogen are all capped, giving formulators a specific compositional target for low-ash lubricants intended for combined electric-motor and transmission lubrication.

records.title: Lubricant composition for speed reducer and speed reducer
records.abstract: The present invention provides a lubricant composition for a speed reducer, which has a long service life at high temperature and low input torque at low temperature and is used for an eccentric oscillating planetary gear type speed reducer, and a speed reducer. A lubricant composition for eccentric oscillating planetary gear reducers comprises (a) a base oil comprising a synthetic oil, (b) a hydrocarbon-based wax, and (c) at least one calcium salt selected from the group consisting of a calcium salt of petroleum sulfonic acid, a calcium salt of an alkyl aromatic sulfonic acid, a calcium salt of an oxidized wax, an overbased calcium salt of petroleum sulfonic acid, an overbased calcium salt of an alkyl aromatic sulfonic acid, and an overbased calcium salt of an oxidized wax.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricant composition intended for eccentric oscillating planetary gear type speed reducers, addressing the stated goals of long service life at high temperature and low input torque at low temperature. The composition comprises (a) a base oil containing a synthetic oil, (b) a hydrocarbon-based wax, and (c) at least one calcium salt selected from calcium salts of petroleum sulfonic acid, alkyl aromatic sulfonic acid, and oxidized wax, including their overbased forms. Independent claim 1 defines this three-component composition; dependent claims add embodiments such as polyethylene or polypropylene wax, wax content of 0.1–20 mass%, synthetic hydrocarbon oil, base oil kinematic viscosity at 40 °C of 20–300 mm²/s, and preference for alkyl aromatic sulfonate calcium salts. Claim 7 covers a speed reducer enclosing the composition. The source is abstract and claims only; no experimental performance data are supplied, so the stated high-temperature life and low-temperature torque behavior are not demonstrated in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a formulation space combining synthetic base oil, hydrocarbon wax, and specific calcium sulfonate/wax salts for eccentric oscillating planetary reducers, giving a concrete compositional target for lubricant development and infringement or design-around analysis.

records.summary: The disclosure describes a siloxane compound represented by formula (1), in which silicon atoms bear substituents X1 (hydrogen, C1–C12 alkyl, or a polyoxyalkylene group of formula (2)) and the structure includes alkylene Y, divalent organic group Z1 bonded to silicon via a carbon–silicon bond and to oxygen, with indices p (0–13), q and r (0–16), n (2–4), and a (0–11), and at least one of q and r having an average number of 1.4 or more. A dependent claim states that the compound has a viscosity index greater than 200 and a residue after heating at 140°C for 100 hours and then at 250°C for 700 hours of less than 20%. The disclosure further describes a lubricating oil composition containing (A) 30–95 mass% of the siloxane compound, (B) a hydrocarbon lubricating oil, and at least one of (C) an extreme pressure additive and (D) an antioxidant. Dependent claims also cover lubricants, greases, emulsions, and lubricating methods using the compound or composition. Only the abstract and claims were retrieved, so no experimental data or description are available to verify the reported properties.

records.title: High power shielded busbar for electric vehicle charging and power distribution
records.abstract: A unitary busbar provides power from one connection point in an electric vehicle to another connection point. The unitary busbar includes a central solid core conductor, an insulation layer over the solid core conductor, and an electromagnetic shield fitted around the insulator. The unitary busbar is capable of being bent into specific configurations that allow it to conform to the body of an electric vehicle.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a unitary busbar for electric-vehicle power distribution that combines a solid core conductor, an insulation layer, and a conductive shielding layer compressed against the insulation, with at least one connector formed from the core conductor itself. In the independent system claim, the busbar is bent to conform to the vehicle interior, connects a first connection point to a second connection point at the opposite end, and the shielding layer is grounded to the vehicle through a rigid ground conductor. The independent method claim covers forging at least one conductor end into a connector, applying insulation, compressing an outer shield to form a unitary busbar, bending it, and grounding the shield via a rigid ground conductor. Dependent claims add details such as a charge port as the first connection point, a battery connector as the second, forged flattened connectors with through holes, aluminum or copper conductors and shields, XLPE/PVC/silicone insulation, and approximate dimensions of 200 mm² conductor cross-section with about 1 mm insulation and shield thickness. Certain dependent claims state the busbar can support 350 kW charging at 400 V while keeping the shielding layer at about 100 °C or less; these are claim features, not demonstrated experimental results in the supplied text.

records.title: Power battery, busbar component of power battery and method thereof
records.abstract: Disclosed are a power battery, a busbar component of the power battery and a method thereof. The busbar component comprises a busbar assembly. The busbar assembly comprises a busbar body, a first insulating layer and a second insulating layer. The busbar body is connected with one side of the first insulating layer facing a battery cell module, is integrated with a sampling line, and the sampling line is manufactured by a mechanical cutting and unloading process. The second insulating layer is attached to the first insulating layer and covers the sampling line, and the second insulating layer and the busbar body are on a same side of the first insulating layer and are arranged in a staggered manner. The cost is lowered, the process cycle of product is shortened, the production efficiency is improved, the applicability gets wider, the production process and the assembling process are simplified.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a busbar component for a power battery in which a busbar body is attached to one side of a first insulating layer facing the battery cell module, and a sampling line is integrated on that same side of the first insulating layer, the sampling line being made by a mechanical cutting and unloading process. A second insulating layer is attached to the first insulating layer, covers the sampling line, and is arranged in a staggered manner relative to the busbar body on the same side of the first insulating layer. The first insulating layer has reserved holes corresponding to the busbar body, and the busbar assembly is described as connected to the cell module at those reserved holes by laser welding. The abstract states that the arrangement lowers cost, shortens the product process cycle, improves production efficiency, widens applicability, and simplifies production and assembly processes; these are stated advantages rather than measured results. The source covers the abstract and all 19 claims only, with no description or figures, so the summary is limited to claim and abstract content.
records.why_it_matters: Integrating the sampling line into the first insulating layer by mechanical cutting and unloading, rather than as a separate routed component, is the claimed architectural move that could reduce part count and assembly steps in busbar-to-cell-module interconnection.

records.abstract: Translated from Korean 넓은 온도 범위에 있어서 액정성을 나타내고, 낮은 운동 마찰 계수를 유지하고, 도전성을 갖고, 증발, 분해 등에 의한 손실이 거의 없고, 청결한 외관을 갖고, 형광을 발하기 때문에, 열화나 누설을 즉시 발견할 수 있다는 특성을 겸비하는 도전성 윤활제를 제공한다.  식 (1): [식 중, R 11 및 R 21 은 동일하거나 또는 다르고, 수소 또는 기 -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR(R은 직쇄 또는 분지쇄의 C n H 2n+1 이며, 4≤n≤12이며, R'는 메틸 또는 에틸임)이며, R 12 , R 13 , R 22 및 R 23 은 동일하거나 또는 다르고, 기 -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR(R은 직쇄 또는 분지쇄의 C n H 2n+1 이며, 4≤n≤12이며, R'는 메틸 또는 에틸임)이다]로 표시되는 화합물 (1)을 적어도 1종 포함하는 도전성 윤활제로 한다. A conductive lubricant is provided which has the characteristics of exhibiting liquid crystallinity over a wide temperature range, maintaining a low coefficient of kinetic friction, being conductive, experiencing little loss due to evaporation, decomposition, etc., having a clean appearance, and fluorescing so that deterioration or leakage can be immediately detected. Formula (1): A conductive lubricant comprising at least one compound (1) represented by [wherein R 11 and R 21 are the same or different and are hydrogen or a group -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR (R is a linear or branched C n H 2n+1 , 4≤n≤12, and R' is methyl or ethyl), and R 12 , R 13 , R 22 and R 23 are the same or different and are a group -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR (R is a linear or branched C n H 2n+1 , 4≤n≤12, and R' is methyl or ethyl)].
records.summary: The disclosure describes a conductive lubricant composition combining a two-ring liquid crystal compound of formula (1) with a three-ring liquid crystal compound of formula (2), at a mass ratio of 95:5 to 15:85. The abstract states the intended characteristics are liquid crystallinity over a wide temperature range, a low coefficient of kinetic friction, electrical conductivity, little loss from evaporation or decomposition, a clean appearance, and fluorescence enabling immediate detection of deterioration or leakage. Formula (1) uses terminal groups -OCH2CH2CH(R')CH2CH2OR with R as linear or branched CnH2n+1 and R' as methyl or ethyl; the claims allow 1≤n≤20, while the abstract states 4≤n≤12. Dependent claims add narrower ranges, specific three-ring structures (formulae 3–5), a two-ring-rich embodiment, and residual-rate criteria. No experimental data, measured conductivities, friction values, or comparative results are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed residual-rate limits (≥95% after 600 h at 100°C, and ≥95% after 1,000 h at 25°C and 10^-5 Pa) frame the composition as targeting low-volatility, long-life lubrication for sealed or vacuum-adjacent hardware such as encapsulated bearings, though the source does not report measured values.

records.summary: The disclosure describes a conductive lubricant composition based on liquid-crystal compounds intended to exhibit liquid crystallinity over a wide temperature range while maintaining a low coefficient of kinetic friction and electrical conductivity. The composition combines at least one two-ring liquid-crystal compound of formula (1) with at least one three-ring compound of formula (2) and at least one three-ring compound of formula (3), in a mass ratio of the sum of these compounds from 60:40 to 4:96. The abstract further states that the lubricant experiences little loss from evaporation or decomposition, has a clean appearance, and fluoresces so that deterioration or leakage can be detected immediately. The claims define the compound structures and mixing ratio, with dependent claims narrowing substituent chain lengths and specifying content ranges for the two-ring compound (4–40 wt%) and the formula (3) compound (20–64 wt%). A further claim covers a bearing encapsulated with the lubricant composition. No experimental performance data are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed combination of liquid-crystal base compounds with a specified two-ring/three-ring mixing ratio is directed at a lubricant that is both conductive and self-indicating via fluorescence, which could allow early detection of lubricant degradation or leakage in encapsulated bearing applications.

records.title: Synthetic industrial gear lubricant composition and preparation method thereof
assignees: 中国石油天然气股份有限公司
records.abstract: The invention discloses a synthetic industrial gear lubricating oil composition which comprises the following components in percentage by mass: the synthetic industrial gear lubricating oil composition has excellent extreme pressure antiwear performance and micro-point corrosion resistance, and meanwhile, the lubricating oil composition also has excellent oxidation stability, viscosity temperature performance, low temperature performance and the like, and can meet the lubrication of industrial closed gears under the working conditions of high load, extremely high temperature, extremely low temperature and humidity, thereby effectively lubricating and protecting gears and bearings, prolonging the service life of a gear box and achieving the purposes of saving energy and reducing consumption.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a synthetic industrial gear lubricant composition intended for closed industrial gears operating under high load, very high or very low temperature, and humid conditions. The composition consists of 0.1–2.0 wt% sulfur-containing extreme-pressure antiwear agent, 0.1–1.0 wt% phosphorus-containing antiwear agent, 0.1–0.5 wt% antioxidant, 0.1–1.0 wt% ashless dispersant, 0.1–0.5 wt% rust inhibitor, and the balance base oil. The base oil is at least one of polyolefin, ester, or polyether synthetic oil, with dependent claims specifying metallocene-catalyzed poly-α-olefin and pentaerythritol ester or diester oils. A preparation method is also described: blending the base oil with the additives in a stainless steel kettle with stirring at 50–60 °C for 2–4 h. The abstract asserts excellent extreme-pressure antiwear performance, micro-pitting corrosion resistance, oxidation stability, viscosity-temperature behavior, and low-temperature performance, but no measured test data are supplied in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a fully additized synthetic gear-oil formulation with specified additive treat-rate ranges and a low-temperature blending procedure, giving a concrete compositional basis for formulators targeting combined extreme-pressure, antiwear, and corrosion protection in synthetic industrial gear oils.

records.abstract: Translated from Korean A conductive lubricant is provided which has the characteristics of exhibiting liquid crystallinity over a wide temperature range, maintaining a low coefficient of kinetic friction, being conductive, experiencing little loss due to evaporation, decomposition, etc., having a clean appearance, and fluorescing so that deterioration or leakage can be immediately detected. Formula (1): A conductive lubricant comprising at least one compound (1) represented by [wherein R 11 and R 21 are the same or different and are hydrogen or a group -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR (R is a linear or branched C n H 2n+1, 4≤n≤12, and R' is methyl or ethyl), and R 12 , R 13 , R 22 and R 23 are the same or different and are a group -OCH 2 CH 2 CH(R')CH 2 CH 2 OR (R is a linear or branched C n H 2n+1 , 4≤n≤12, and R' is methyl or ethyl)].
records.summary: The disclosure describes a conductive lubricant built around at least one compound of formula (1), a stilbene-type structure bearing terminal and side-chain groups of the form -OCH2CH2CH(R')CH2CH2OR, where R is a linear or branched CnH2n+1 with 4≤n≤12 and R' is methyl or ethyl. According to the abstract, the intended characteristics are liquid crystallinity over a wide temperature range, a low coefficient of kinetic friction, electrical conductivity, low loss from evaporation or decomposition, a clean appearance, and fluorescence enabling prompt detection of deterioration or leakage. The claims state that the compound can exhibit a smectic liquid crystal phase from -50°C to +300°C, and that a cell with 1 cm2 electrode area and 5 μm inter-electrode distance shows a conductivity of 0.07 μA or more at 5 V over 30°C to 300°C. Dependent claims add positional substitution details, a trans (gigatrans) configuration relative to the -CH=CH- group, a carbon- and metal-free composition, and use of the lubricant on contacting machine elements. Only the abstract and claims were retrieved, so no experimental data or description content is available to verify these properties.
records.why_it_matters: The disclosure describes combining lubrication, electrical conduction, and fluorescence in a single liquid-crystalline material, which could allow a machine element to be lubricated and electrically contacted at the same time while making leakage or degradation visible under UV inspection.

records.abstract: The present invention relates to a lubricating oil composition with improved lubricating performance and cooling performance and a method for manufacturing the same, and more specifically, to a lubricating oil composition with improved lubricating performance and cooling performance and a method for manufacturing the same, wherein the lubricating oil composition can be applied to various local environments to improve lubricating performance and cooling efficiency, thereby improving the output and fuel efficiency of an internal combustion engine in which lubricating oil is used, and improve eco-friendliness such as noise prevention or soot generation suppression, thereby significantly increasing not only the engine use of the internal combustion engine but also the utilization of various industrial groups.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a lubricating oil composition intended to improve both lubrication and cooling performance, and a method for making it. The composition combines a base lubricating oil, a cooling activator comprising water-soluble silicate (SiO3), and an anti-wear improver comprising molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), with the weights of these three components constrained by a stated relationship. Independent claims also cover a manufacturing method with sequential mixing steps: lubricating oil plus viscosity index improver and pour point depressant, then functional fluid, then extreme-pressure improver, accelerator, cooling activator, and anti-wear improver. The abstract asserts applicability across local environments and potential improvements in engine output, fuel efficiency, noise prevention, and soot suppression, but no measured performance data are provided in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed weight relationship among base oil, silicate cooling activator, and MoS2 anti-wear agent defines a compositional design constraint that formulators would need to satisfy, rather than a demonstrated performance window.

records.abstract: The present invention concerns the use of at least one polyorganosiloxane to release air from a lubricant composition comprising at least one base oil, when lubricating at least one moving part of an electric or hybrid vehicle.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a method for releasing air from a lubricant composition used to lubricate moving parts in the propulsion system of an electric or hybrid vehicle. The lubricant comprises at least one base oil and at least one polyorganosiloxane, and the moving part is described as rotating at 1000 to 15000 rpm. The claims state that the composition can exhibit an initial variation in air volume, measured per NF ISO 12152, below 6% or below 5%, and that bubbling losses in the lubrication system can be reduced by at least 10%. Polyorganosiloxanes are described as selectable from polydimethylsiloxanes, used at 0.0005 to 2% by weight, with base oils at 4 to 50 mm2/s kinematic viscosity at 100°C and at least 70% by weight of the composition. The available text is limited to the abstract and claims; no description, figures, or experimental data were retrieved, so reported values are claim features rather than demonstrated results.
records.why_it_matters: For electric-vehicle drivetrains operating at high rotational speeds, entrained air in lubricant can degrade lubrication and increase losses; the disclosure proposes a silicone additive route to deaeration that could be specified as a formulation lever for such systems.

score_details.reason: The claims disclose a method of using polyorganosiloxane (e.g., PDMS) at 0.0005-2 wt% in a base oil to release air from lubricant in electric/hybrid vehicle propulsion systems, targeting rotating parts at 1000-15000 rpm and bearings between rotor and stator. This directly addresses deaeration/anti-foaming for high-speed e-motor lubrication, an adjacent concern to the Advanced Lubricants theme. However, the text is abstract and claims only; no description, examples, or measured data are supplied, so performance claims (e.g., <6% air volume variation per NF ISO 12152, >=10% bubbling loss reduction) are asserted, not demonstrated.

technical_points: Independent claim 1 covers a method of lubricating at least one moving part of an electric or hybrid vehicle propulsion system with a lubricant comprising at least one base oil and at least one polyorganosiloxane, where the moving part rotates at 1000 to 15000 rpm.
Dependent claims specify an initial variation in air volume measured per NF ISO 12152 below 6% (claim 2) or below 5% (claim 3).
The polyorganosiloxane is described as selectable from polydimethylsiloxanes (claims 4, 18), at 0.0005 to 2 wt% (claim 5), or 0.001 to 1.5 wt% (claim 6).
Base oils are described with kinematic viscosity at 100°C of 4 to 50 mm2/s (claim 7) and at least 70 wt% (claim 8), or 80 to 99 wt% (claim 9), of the composition.

Independent claim 16 covers reducing bubbling losses in an electric or hybrid vehicle lubrication system, with dependent claim 17 stating loss reduction of at least 10%; claim 11/20 mention bearings between rotor and stator and the transmission.
limitations: Only the abstract and claims were retrieved; the description, figures, and any examples or experimental data are not available, so no measured performance is confirmed.
The 6%/5% air-volume variation and 10% bubbling-loss reduction are claim features, not demonstrated experimental results in the supplied text.
No comparison to prior art, additive alternatives, or independent validation is provided in the retrieved material.
