records.title: Wavelength-resolved photonic lantern wavefront sensor
assignees: University Of Central Florida Research Foundation, Inc.
records.abstract: A sensor may include one or more photonic lanterns, each including a waveguide structure with a single input waveguide at an input end and two or more output waveguides at an output end, where the two or more output waveguides of each of the one or more photonic lanterns are optically decoupled. A distribution of intensities of light exiting two or more output waveguides of each of the one or more photonic lanterns may correspond to a modal decomposition of input light coupled into the input waveguide of the corresponding one of the one or more photonic lanterns. The sensor may further include one or more spectrometers coupled to the two or more output waveguides of the one or more photonic lanterns to provide a wavelength-resolved modal decomposition of the input light.

score_details.reason: The patent discloses a photonic lantern wavefront sensor that performs wavelength-resolved modal decomposition of input light using spectrometers coupled to decoupled output waveguides, with imaging/adaptive-optics applications (claims 10-23). This is optical/astronomical instrumentation and has no connection to the team's tracked topics of thermal management, plating/contact surfaces, high-speed connectivity, aluminum/dissimilar joining, battery interconnects, or lubricants. The claims are complete and concrete in mechanism, but no measured performance, figures, or description are supplied, and no tracked engineering problem is addressed.

claims: 1 . A sensor comprising: one or more photonic lanterns, each of the one or more photonic lanterns including a waveguide structure with an input waveguide at an input end and two or more output waveguides at an output end, wherein the two or more output waveguides of each of the one or more photonic lanterns are optically decoupled, wherein a distribution of intensities of light exiting the two or more output waveguides of each of the one or more photonic lanterns corresponds to a modal decomposition of input light coupled into the input waveguide of a corresponding one of the one or more photonic lanterns; and one or more spectrometers coupled to the two or more output waveguides of the one or more photonic lanterns to provide a wavelength-resolved modal decomposition of the input light.

2 . The sensor of claim 1 , further comprising: a controller communicatively coupled to the one or more spectrometers, the controller including one or more processors configured to execute program instructions causing the one or more processors to: determine wavelength-resolved measurements of at least one of an amplitude or a phase associated with modes of the input light.

3 . The sensor of claim 1 , wherein the one or more photonic lanterns comprise two photonic lanterns, wherein base modes associated with the modal decomposition of each of the two photonic lanterns are different, wherein the sensor further comprises a beamsplitter to receive the input light and direct portions of the input light to the input waveguides of the two photonic lanterns.
4 . The sensor of claim 1 , wherein the one or more photonic lanterns comprise a single photonic lantern.

5 . The sensor of claim 4 , further comprising: a controller communicatively coupled to the one or more spectrometers, the controller including one or more processors configured to execute program instructions causing the one or more processors to: determine wavelength-resolved measurements of at least one of amplitudes or phases associated with modes of the input light.

6 . The sensor of claim 5 , wherein determining the wavelength-resolved measurements of at least one of the amplitudes and the phases associated with the modes of the input light comprises: determining the wavelength-resolved measurements of at least one of the amplitudes and the phases associated with the modes of the input light using a machine learning algorithm.

records.title: Method for manufacturing a busbar and such a busbar
records.abstract: A method for manufacturing a busbar ( 1 ), in particular a laminated busbar ( 1 ), configured for mounting an electronic component, in particular a passive electronic component such as a capacitor, on the busbar ( 1 ), comprising: providing a first conductive layer ( 11 ) made from aluminum, providing a first connector element ( 15 ) for connecting the first conductive layer ( 11 ) and the electronic component, wherein the first connector element ( 15 ) is at least partially covered with nickel and/or tin, and creating an bond between the first conductive layer ( 11 ) and the first connector element ( 15 ) by laser welding.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a method for manufacturing a busbar, particularly a laminated busbar, configured for mounting an electronic component such as a capacitor. A first aluminum conductive layer is provided along with a first connector element at least partially covered with nickel and/or tin, and a bond between them is created by laser welding. The independent claim further requires a second aluminum conductive layer and a second connector element at least partially covered with nickel and/or selenium, laser-welded to the second layer, with the layers arranged so the second connector element reaches through the first conductive layer, for example through a corresponding recess. The source is limited to the abstract and claims; no description, figures, or experimental data are available, so no measured performance is reported.
records.why_it_matters: The disclosure describes a laser-welding route for joining nickel- or tin-coated connector elements to aluminum busbar layers, which is relevant to producing aluminum-based laminated busbars for capacitor mounting without relying on the connector elements being aluminum.

score_details.reason: Claims disclose a concrete manufacturing method for aluminum laminated busbars: Ni/Sn-coated connector elements laser-welded to aluminum conductive layers, with a second layer/connector reaching through a recess in the first. This directly addresses aluminum-to-dissimilar joining and contact-surface plating for power interconnect hardware, relevant to the team's joining and plating topics. Mechanism is specific (plating thickness 1-50 µm, dual-sided laser seams, form-fitting bushings), but no measured outcomes, weld strength, or reliability data are supplied, and the description/figures are absent, limiting quality and confidence. Novelty is plausible but cannot be judged versus prior art from claims alone.
evidence: the nickel plating and/or the tin plating has a thickness between 1 pm and 50 pm
limitations: No measured weld strength, electrical resistance, thermal cycling, or reliability data provided
Description and figures not supplied; only abstract and claims available
No comparison to prior art, so novelty over existing aluminum busbar joining methods is unestablished
Claim 1 lists 'selenium' for the second connector coating, likely a translation artifact; actual coating chemistry uncertain
No process parameters (laser power, speed, wavelength) beyond qualitative statements

records.title: Busbar for energy storage device
records.abstract: A laminated busbar for interconnecting electrical storage devices, comprising an insulating layer and at least one conductive band arranged on the insulating layer, the at least one conductive band comprising a succession of repeating conductor patterns, each conductor pattern defining a cluster having a first terminal and a second terminal for connection to an energy storage device. The laminated busbar also comprises a first terminator coupled to the first terminal and a second terminator coupled to the second terminal, the first and second terminators configured to connect to terminals of the energy storage device.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a laminated busbar for interconnecting electrical storage devices, such as battery cells. The busbar has an insulating layer with at least one conductive band made from pre-stamped metal coil, the band containing a repeating succession of conductor patterns, each defining a cluster with a first and second terminal for connection to a storage device. First and second terminators couple to those terminals to connect to the device terminals, and the insulating layer is formed of top and bottom layers that laminate the conductive band between them, with openings allowing access to each terminator from both sides. The claims further describe longitudinal and transverse arrangement of conductors and clusters, polarity assignments of terminals, and configurations with one laminated band plus two termination conductors or a pair of laminated bands joined by a junction bar. No measured performance data or experimental results are provided in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed laminated, pre-stamped-coil construction with dual-side access openings may simplify welding of busbar terminators to cell poles and support scalable, repeating cluster layouts for multi-cell storage modules.

This directly addresses battery interconnect layout, welding access, and polarity routing. However, only abstract and claims are supplied; no measured electrical, thermal, or reliability data, materials, current ratings, or comparative prior-art discussion, so quality and novelty remain moderate.

records.title: Electrical busbar with alignment features
records.abstract: A busbar system is configured to carry current, such as, for example, in a battery system. The busbar system includes two or more busbars, that interface at respective surfaces and are aligned by one or more alignment features. The one or more alignment features may include a boss feature such as a pin or other protrusion, a recess such as a hole, slot, or other recess feature, or both a boss feature and a recess feature. Each busbar may include an alignment feature that engages with the alignment feature of the other busbar to cause, maintain, or otherwise effect alignment. Alignment of the busbars ensures relative position, prevents relative motion, or both. The busbars are engaged with each other by positioning the busbars such that their mating surfaces can engage, and then engaging alignment features of the busbars to provide alignment of the busbars relative to each other.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a busbar system for carrying current, for example in a battery system, in which two or more busbars interface at respective surfaces and are aligned by one or more alignment features. The alignment features may include a boss such as a pin or other protrusion, a recess such as a hole, slot, or other recess, or both. In the claimed arrangement, a first busbar has a hole and a notch along an outer edge of a first surface, and a second busbar has a through-hole and a bent tab on a second surface; a fastener extends through the through-hole into the hole and applies a clamping force between the surfaces. When the hole and through-hole are aligned and the surfaces are in direct electrical contact, the second surface extends along the first surface until the notch is reached, where the second surface bends into the notch via the bent tab. The disclosure describes alignment as ensuring relative position and/or preventing relative motion, but no measured electrical or mechanical performance data are supplied.
records.why_it_matters: The bent-tab-and-notch engagement is described as constraining relative motion of the two busbars in the interface plane, which is an anti-rotation/alignment function that is separate from the fastener's clamping role.

original_evidence.abstract: A busbar system is configured to carry current, such as, for example, in a battery system. The busbar system includes two or more busbars, that interface at respective surfaces and are aligned by one or more alignment features. The one or more alignment features may include a boss feature such as a pin or other protrusion, a recess such as a hole, slot, or other recess feature, or both a boss feature and a recess feature. Each busbar may include an alignment feature that engages with the alignment feature of the other busbar to cause, maintain, or otherwise effect alignment. Alignment of the busbars ensures relative position, prevents relative motion, or both. The busbars are engaged with each other by positioning the busbars such that their mating surfaces can engage, and then engaging alignment features of the busbars to provide alignment of the busbars relative to each other.

records.abstract: Provided is a battery module capable of keeping a joint strength high at a joint between dissimilar metals of a busbar. A battery module 100 of the present invention includes a plurality of battery cells each having cell terminals 1p and 1n, and a busbar 2A joining the terminals of the battery cells 1. The busbar 2A has a plurality of connection face portions 2c1 and 2c2 each connected to a corresponding one of the terminals 1p and 1n of the battery cells 1; a plurality of rising portions each rising from a corresponding one of the plurality of connection face portions 2c1 and 2c2; and a connection portion connecting the plurality of rising portions. The busbar includes a copper portion 2e including copper and an aluminum portion 2f including aluminum, and a joint between the copper portion 2e and the aluminum portion 2f are located on the connection face portion 2c1, 2c2.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a battery module in which multiple battery cells with terminals are joined by busbars that combine a copper portion and an aluminum portion. The busbar has connection face portions that contact the cell terminals, rising portions extending from those faces, and a connection portion linking the rising portions. The copper-aluminum joint is positioned on the connection face portions (independent claims 1, 3, 8) or on the rising portions (independent claim 5), rather than being placed where it would interfere with the terminal joint. The stated aim is to keep joint strength high at the dissimilar-metal joint of the busbar; no measured performance data are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: Placing the copper-aluminum dissimilar-metal joint away from the busbar-to-terminal weld region separates the structural dissimilar-metal joint from the cell-terminal connection, which the disclosure presents as a way to preserve joint strength in a mixed-metal busbar.

records.title: Optimal equalization partitioning with automatic gain adjustment
records.abstract: An optical module configured to electrically connect to a host. A linear equalizer performs equalization on a host equalized signal to create a module equalized signal, and a driver configured to present the module equalized signal from the linear equalizer to an optical conversion device at a magnitude suitable for the optical conversion device. An optical conversion device receives the module equalized signal from the driver, converts the module equalized signal to an optical signal, and transmit the optical signal over an optical channel. Also part of the optical module is an interface which communicates supplemental equalizer settings to the host. A memory stores the supplemental equalizer settings which reflect the optical modules effect on a signal passing through the optical module. A controller oversees communication of the supplemental equalizer settings to the host such that the host uses the supplemental equalizer settings to modify host equalizer settings.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a transmit path in which a host equalizes an outgoing signal and sends it over a host-to-optic-module channel to an optical module. Inside the module, a linear equalizer and a gain unit perform linear equalization and variable linear amplification, with the gain unit automatically adjusting gain to maintain a target modulation amplitude based on transmit host settings, before a driver feeds an electrical-to-optical device that transmits over fiber. The abstract further describes an interface and memory that communicate supplemental equalizer settings reflecting the module's effect on the signal, so the host can modify its own equalizer settings. Dependent claims add features such as joint host/module training, frequency-specific gain adjustment, and operation at 25 Gb/s or more without a CDR in the module. No measured performance data or experimental results are provided in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The described architecture would let the optical module absorb channel and module variation through automatic gain and equalization adjustment, so host equalizer settings need not be retrained when the channel changes, per dependent claim 4.

original_evidence.abstract: An optical module configured to electrically connect to a host. A linear equalizer performs equalization on a host equalized signal to create a module equalized signal, and a driver configured to present the module equalized signal from the linear equalizer to an optical conversion device at a magnitude suitable for the optical conversion device. An optical conversion device receives the module equalized signal from the driver, converts the module equalized signal to an optical signal, and transmit the optical signal over an optical channel. Also part of the optical module is an interface which communicates supplemental equalizer settings to the host. A memory stores the supplemental equalizer settings which reflect the optical modules effect on a signal passing through the optical module. A controller oversees communication of the supplemental equalizer settings to the host such that the host uses the supplemental equalizer settings to modify host equalizer settings.

records.abstract: A correction optical element (COE) for a multi-channeled coherent beam combining (CBC) system that uses a fiber array comprising multiple optical fibers and a single collimation array comprising multiple collimating lenses, for coherent combining of a corresponding array of optical beams directed through the fiber array. The COE is configured for customized and segmented correction of collimation-based optical aberrations, caused at least due to misalignments between each corresponding optical fiber's Lij output end and a center of a corresponding collimating lens Lij.

claims: 1. 2. The COE of claim 1, wherein the COE is configured to segmentally correct, for each output optical beam Bij, any one or more optical aberrations of: pointing errors; focusing/collimation errors; wave-front aberrations; high-order three dimensional aberrations, spatial distribution errors; comatic aberrations; field curvature aberrations, cylinder aberrations; smile errors, manufacturing errors, errors in spaces between collimating lenses in the collimation array.

determining, for each segment CSij of the COE to be fabricated, a required correction design for correcting ah measured optical aberrations of the respective correcting segment CSij, for the specific CBC system and for a particular location and positioning of the COE to be fabricated; fabricating a COE having an array of segments, by configuring each segment of the COE according to its respective required correction design; placing the COE at a determined positioning for optimal aberrations correction such that each correction segment CSij of the COE is positioned in an optimal positioning in respect to the output optical beam Bij; records.abstract: The present invention relates to a functionalized polymer and a composition comprising the same, wherein the functionalized polymer comprises partially or fully saturated polymer having amide, imide and/or ester functionalized moieties, comprising a C_4-5 olefin. The present invention has i) a Mw/Mn of less than 2, ii) a functionality distribution (Fd) of 3.5 or less, and iii) a Mn of 10000 g/mol or more (GPC-PS) of the polymer prior to functionalization. However, when the polymer prior to functionalization is a copolymer of isoprene and butadiene, the Mn of the copolymer is greater than 25000 g/mol (GPC-PS).
records.summary: The disclosure describes functionalized polymers derived from C4–5 olefin polymers that are partially or fully saturated and bear amide, imide and/or ester functional moieties. The pre-functionalization polymer is characterized by Mw/Mn below 2, a functionality distribution (Fd) of 3.5 or less, and Mn of at least 10,000 g/mol by GPC-PS, with a special proviso that isoprene/butadiene copolymers must exceed 25,000 g/mol. The claims further describe a route in which a fully or partially hydrogenated C4–5 conjugated diene polymer is reacted with an acylating agent and then with an amine to form imide and/or amide functionality. Lubricant compositions containing base oil, dispersant, detergent and the functionalized polymer are also claimed, with optional performance targets such as soot-induced wear of 55 mg or less and soot-induced viscosity increase of no more than 12 cSt at 6% soot. No experimental data are supplied in the retrieved abstract and claims, so reported performance is claimed rather than demonstrated.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a narrow molecular-weight-distribution, low-functionality-distribution route to saturated C4–5 olefin polymers with amide/imide/ester groups, which is the architectural lever proposed for controlling dispersancy and soot handling in heavy-duty diesel lubricants.

records.title: Cylindrical stamped electrical power terminal
assignees: 美商Ｆｃｉ美國有限責任公司
records.abstract: High current, light, and low-cost electrical power terminals that can withstand many mating cycles. A socket or a pin may be formed from a monolithic metal sheet, which may be stamped and formed into a terminal with a hollow portion, such as a cylindrical barrel. Features defining the radius of the barrel may be stamped in the sheet with high precision. The socket and the pin are shaped such that the positions of the mating contact surfaces of each terminal, and therefore the interference between them, are positioned based on these features. The terminals may have a low and precise interference, enabling the terminals to be designed with a low contact force that enables a long lifespan, such as 10,000 mating cycles. The terminals may have a high current capacity, such as 50 A or higher, and may be used in high current applications, such as a charging station or an electric vehicle, or in an application that calls for charging or discharging a battery.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a high-current electrical power terminal made from a single stamped metal sheet formed into a hollow portion (such as a cylindrical barrel) around an embedded axis, with a mounting contact and a mating contact on the outer portion of the hollow. In one family of claims, a complementary terminal has multiple deflectable beams extending from a base parallel to the axis, arranged around the axis with mating contacts facing inward. The abstract states that stamping features that define the barrel radius with high precision allows low, precise interference and low contact force, which the disclosure associates with long lifespan (e.g., 10,000 mating cycles) and high current capacity (e.g., 50 A or higher). Claim features recite dimensional ranges and ratios, but the source provides no experimental data or measured performance.
records.why_it_matters: The claimed approach ties terminal contact force and interference to stamped sheet features rather than machined geometry, which could allow a stamped, low-cost terminal design to target many mating cycles and high current in EV or charging-station connectors.

original_evidence.abstract: High current, light, and low-cost electrical power terminals that can withstand many mating cycles. A socket or a pin may be formed from a monolithic metal sheet, which may be stamped and formed into a terminal with a hollow portion, such as a cylindrical barrel. Features defining the radius of the barrel may be stamped in the sheet with high precision. The socket and the pin are shaped such that the positions of the mating contact surfaces of each terminal, and therefore the interference between them, are positioned based on these features. The terminals may have a low and precise interference, enabling the terminals to be designed with a low contact force that enables a long lifespan, such as 10,000 mating cycles. The terminals may have a high current capacity, such as 50 A or higher, and may be used in high current applications, such as a charging station or an electric vehicle, or in an application that calls for charging or discharging a battery.

records.title: Al-Cu aluminum alloy, preparation method thereof and heat-resistant cable
assignees: 崇义绿冶新能源有限公司
records.abstract: The invention provides an Al-Cu aluminum alloy, which contains Al, cu with the mass percentage content of 0.01-0.6%, mg with the mass percentage content of 0-0.7%, si with the mass percentage content of 0-0.3%, RE with the mass percentage content of 0-0.2%, ge with the mass percentage content of 0-0.3% and Nb with the mass percentage content of 0-0.2%. The invention also provides a preparation method of the Al-Cu aluminum alloy and a heat-resistant cable. According to the invention, on the basis of keeping low cost and low process complexity, the Al-Cu aluminum alloy for the heat-resistant cable with excellent comprehensive performance (especially mechanical performance, conductive performance and heat resistance) can be obtained by adopting less elements.
records.summary: The disclosure describes an Al-Cu-based aluminum alloy intended for heat-resistant cable conductors, formulated with a deliberately small set of alloying elements to keep cost and process complexity low. The alloy contains Al plus 0.01–0.6 wt% Cu, 0–0.7 wt% Mg, 0–0.3 wt% Si, 0–0.2 wt% RE, 0–0.3 wt% Ge and 0–0.2 wt% Nb, with dependent claims adding optional elements such as Sr, Bi, Be, Zn, Ni, Cd, Co, Ca, Sc, Sn, Fe, B and Zr and specifying element mass ratios. A preparation method is also described: heating an aluminum source to form aluminum liquid, adding the alloying elements with a second heating step, refining and skimming with composition verification, then continuous casting and rolling, drawing to wire, and aging. The aging step is described in a dependent claim as two-stage aging (100–150 °C for 1–150 h, then 150–250 °C for 1–100 h). A heat-resistant cable is claimed comprising a cable core made of the alloy and an insulating layer. The abstract asserts excellent comprehensive performance, especially mechanical, conductive and heat-resistance properties, but no measured property values are supplied in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The disclosure defines a low-alloying-element Al-Cu conductor composition and a cast-roll-draw-age process route aimed at heat-resistant cable cores, giving a concrete compositional window and processing sequence that could guide alloy design or freedom-to-operate review for heat-resistant aluminum conductors.

score_details.reason: The patent discloses an Al-Cu alloy composition (Cu 0.01-0.6%, optional Mg/Si/RE/Ge/Nb) and a continuous casting-rolling, drawing and two-stage aging process, aimed at heat-resistant cable conductors with good mechanical, conductive and heat-resistance performance. This is relevant to aluminum conductor materials adjacent to the team's Aluminum & Dissimilar Joining and thermal topics, but the text gives no measured conductivity, tensile strength, heat-resistance data, or comparison to prior alloys, so quality and novelty cannot be substantiated. Claims are broad composition ranges with many optional elements, and the abstract only asserts 'excellent comprehensive performance' without evidence.

records.abstract: Translated from Korean 저 S 해양 연료 트렁크 피스톤 디젤 엔진 윤활제는 과염기화된 금속 세제; 아연 다이하이드로카빌다이티오포스페이트; 임의적으로, 아민계 산화방지제; 및 붕산화된 무회 분산제를 포함한다.  상기 윤활제는 개선된 열 및 산화 안정성 및 개선된 고온 세정능을 나타낸다. Low S Marine Fuel Trunk Piston Diesel Engine Lubricant is an overbased metal detergent; zinc dihydrocarbyldithiophosphate; Optionally, amine-based antioxidants; and borated ashless dispersants. These lubricants exhibit improved thermal and oxidation stability and improved high temperature cleanability.
records.summary: The disclosure describes a low-sulfur marine fuel trunk piston diesel engine lubricant composition built around a Group I and/or Group II base oil making up at least 50% by mass, combined with overbased metal detergents (metal salts of hydrocarbyl-substituted sulfonic acids and salicylic acids), 50–500 ppm by weight (as P) of primary and/or secondary zinc dihydrocarbyldithiophosphate, optionally 400 ppm or less (as N) of amine-based antioxidant, and 10–200 ppm by weight (as B) of borated ashless dispersant. The composition is described as having a TBN from 5 to less than 20 mg KOH/g. The abstract states the lubricants exhibit improved thermal and oxidation stability and improved high-temperature cleanability, though the available text does not include experimental data demonstrating these effects. A related independent claim covers a method of operating a four-stroke trunk piston engine fueled with low-sulfur marine fuel and lubricated with the disclosed composition. Only the abstract and claims were retrieved; the description and figures are not included, and the English text may be machine translated.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a low-TBN (5 to <20 mg KOH/g) formulation window that pairs overbased sulfonate/salicylate detergents with tightly bounded zinc DDP, amine antioxidant, and borated dispersant levels, giving formulators a specific additive-balance target for low-sulfur marine trunk piston service.

records.abstract: Translated from Korean 2-행정 또는 4-행정 선박 엔진 윤활제용 첨가제 팩키지는 윤활 점도 오일; 90/10 내지 10/90 비(비누의 mmol로서 표시됨)의 살리실레이트 세제 및 설폰에이트 세제; 및 1 내지 10 질량%의 하이드로카빌페놀-알데하이드 축합물을 포함한다. Additive packages for 2-stroke or 4-stroke marine engine lubricants include lubricating viscosity oils; salicylate and sulfonate detergents in a ratio of 90/10 to 10/90 (expressed as mmol of soap); and 1 to 10% by mass of a hydrocarbylphenol-aldehyde condensate.
records.summary: The disclosure describes an additive package for 2-stroke or 4-stroke marine engine lubricants that combines a lubricating-viscosity oil with two overbased detergents—a metal hydroxybenzoate (salicylate) detergent (A) and a metal sulfonate detergent (B)—in a soap-mmol ratio of 90:10 to 10:90, plus 1 to 10 mass% of an oil-soluble hydrocarbylphenol-aldehyde condensate (C). Independent claim 1 recites the package with less than 50 mass% lubricating oil, at least 40 mass% total of (A) and (B), and 1–10 mass% of (C). Dependent claims narrow (C) to 3–6 mass% and the (A):(B) ratio to 80:20–20:80, and specify overbased calcium salicylate, overbased calcium sulfonate, and a methylene-bridged alkylphenol whose hydroxyl may be capped. Claim 3 covers a finished lubricant with at least 50 mass% base oil and less than 50 mass% of the package, with TBN by ASTM D2896 of 10–120 mg KOH/g for 2-stroke compositions and 25–60 mg KOH/g for 4-stroke compositions. A method claim covers supplying the composition to the piston/cylinder of a cross-head marine diesel engine. No experimental performance data are supplied in the retrieved text.
records.why_it_matters: The claims define a compositional window—salicylate/sulfonate soap ratio and condensate loading—that formulators can use to target marine cylinder-lubricant TBN ranges while balancing salicylate and sulfonate detergent chemistries.

records.title: Optical chip, laser radar and mobile device
assignees: 深圳市速腾聚创科技有限公司
records.abstract: The embodiment of the application discloses an optical chip, a laser radar and movable equipment, wherein the optical chip comprises a cladding, an edge coupler array, a first connecting waveguide module and a second connecting waveguide module. The edge coupler array comprises a first coupler array, a second coupler array and a third coupler array which are respectively positioned on two opposite sides of the first coupler array, and the second coupler array and the third coupler array comprise two edge couplers. The first connecting waveguide module is respectively connected with two edge couplers in the second coupler array. The second connecting waveguide modules are respectively connected with two edge couplers in the third coupler array. Compared with the prior art, the optical paths of the two edge couplers in the edge coupler array are conducted through the waveguide, the first connecting waveguide module and the second connecting waveguide module can be designed to be shorter, the occupied area is smaller, the area utilization rate of the optical chip can be improved, and the cost is reduced.

score_details.reason: The patent discloses a photonic integrated circuit layout for a lidar optical chip: an edge coupler array split into first/second/third sub-arrays, with connecting waveguide modules (including optical splitters) routing the two edge couplers in the second and third arrays to shorten waveguide runs and reduce chip area. Claims further cover photodetection modules, wavelength division multiplexers for twin-wavelength lidar, and a lidar/mobile device incorporating the chip. This is adjacent to the team's High-Speed Connectivity theme (optical/optoelectronic interconnect and coupling), but it is a lidar transceiver chip rather than a data-communications connectivity component, so relevance is moderate. records.title: Optical fiber geometric parameter testing system and testing method
assignees: 武汉镱得飞光电技术有限公司
records.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of optical fiber geometric parameter testing, and provides an optical fiber geometric parameter testing system and an optical fiber geometric parameter testing method, wherein the optical fiber geometric parameter testing system comprises a light source, a Dammann grating, an optical fiber clamp unit, a lens unit and a detector, and also comprises a controller connected with the detector, wherein the Dammann grating, the optical fiber clamp unit, the lens unit and the detector are sequentially arranged along the optical axis direction of the light source; the optical fiber clamp unit is used for clamping a plurality of optical fibers to be tested, the optical fibers to be tested are distributed along the direction perpendicular to the optical axis of the light source and form an optical fiber array to be tested, and the axial directions of the optical fibers to be tested are parallel to the direction of the optical axis of the light source; the optical fiber array tester comprises a light source, a lens unit, a detector, a controller and a plurality of optical fibers, wherein the light beam emitted by the light source is split by the Dammann grating to form a plurality of sub-beams, the sub-beams are irradiated on one end face of the optical fibers to be tested in a one-to-one correspondence mode, the lens unit is used for imaging the other end face of the optical fibers to be tested, the detector is used for collecting imaging images of the lens unit and storing the imaging images into the controller, and the controller obtains geometric parameters of the optical fiber array to be tested through image processing, so that batch testing of a large number of optical fibers is realized.
records.summary: The disclosure describes an optical fiber geometric parameter testing system and method intended for batch measurement of multiple fibers. A light source beam is split by a Dammann grating into multiple sub-beams that illuminate one end face of a fiber array under test in one-to-one correspondence; the fibers are held by a clamp unit with their axes parallel to the light source optical axis and distributed perpendicular to it. A lens unit images the other end faces onto a detector, and a controller processes the captured images to derive geometric parameters of the fiber array. The claims also describe optional collimation, switchable filters and imaging lenses, and adjustable mounts for the fiber clamp and detector. No measured performance data or experimental results are provided in the retrieved abstract and claims.
records.why_it_matters: The Dammann-grating beam splitting combined with one-to-one fiber illumination and imaging suggests a parallel optical architecture aimed at testing many fibers in a single acquisition rather than sequentially, which is the core engineering implication for throughput-oriented fiber geometry inspection.

technical_points: Independent claim 1 defines a system with a light source, Dammann grating, fiber clamp unit, lens unit, detector and controller arranged sequentially along the light source optical axis, with the fiber array oriented perpendicular to that axis and fiber axes parallel to it.

The Dammann grating splits the source beam into multiple sub-beams that irradiate one end face of the fibers under test in one-to-one correspondence; the lens unit images the opposite end faces and the controller derives geometric parameters via image processing.

Dependent claim 2 specifies that the sub-beams form a lattice-like focused spot array overlapping the fiber array, with focused spot diameter greater than or equal to the fiber diameter; claim 3 specifies coincidence of spot center and fiber axial center.

Dependent claims 4-7 add an optical fiber collimator between source and grating, a switchable filter unit, a switchable imaging lens group, and first and second adjusting frames for the fiber clamp array and detector, all controller-connected.

Independent method claim 8 recites arranging fibers on the clamp unit, splitting the beam through the Dammann grating for one-to-one end-face illumination, imaging the other end faces onto the detector, and image-processing the captured images to obtain array geometric parameters; claims 9-10 add filter and lens switching steps.

## This week in brief

- **Co-packaged optics (CPO) moved from concept toward platform integration.** Celestica announced the DS6005, a 102.4Tbps, 64×1.6TbE, fully liquid-cooled ORv3 switch built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 Davisson, with optical engines on the ASIC package and field-replaceable external lasers ([Celestica DS6005](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC showed a live ORv3 compute system with TeraPHY optical engines and telemetry ([PR Newswire](https://news.google.?oc=5)). Intel claimed sole volume production of InP-on-300mm-silicon and targets below 5 pJ/bit ([BigGo Finance](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTE13VnE1X0N4SktSZm5GSGpRd1VhSDJaSHEyS3R3M0dfVFcyb29mc1NlclI1aF9SbmE2SzhqZmYwTm84ZmtuZFE2U0xhZXd2YWZrVXpnUjlCS3FtRk5xT3dOSi1tVWRzRlhwTmtUMWRvS1NKaUMzSWc?oc=5)).
- **Busbar thermal risk got a simulation-based surrogate.** An interpretable XGBoost model trained on 3D electro-thermal FEA of bolted switchgear joints reached R²=0.990±0.005 and RMSE=1.877±0.542 K, with load current and contact resistance dominant in SHAP; the authors state it is geometry-specific and not experimentally validated ([Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmech.2026.1904437)).
- **WAAM review positioned arc welding as its metallurgical base.** The review covers G/R grain control, transfer modes and defects, noting CMT's low heat input and low spatter versus independent wire-feed/arc-power control in GTAW and PAW ([Materials](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma19204362)).
- **L-PBF control was demonstrated only in simulation.** A data-based predictive FIR controller cut threshold-exceeding melt-pool samples by 99.98% in one layer, evaluated in MATLAB rather than on the printer ([Int J Adv Manuf Technol](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19180-5)).
- **Plating studies offered process trade-offs.** A 1994 electroless nickel study found the ammonium bath slowest (13 µm/h) but the only one reaching six turnovers without precipitation, while lithium was fastest initially but precipitated ([Finishing and Coating](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3049-the-effect-of-monovalent-cations-on-electroless-nickel-plating)).

## Themes to watch

CPO is converging on liquid-cooled ORv3 racks with external lasers and telemetry-based validation, but vendor claims of power and latency gains remain unquantified. Copper interconnect reliability is being addressed through both design guidance (plating thickness, joint torque, temperature rise) and simulation surrogates. Additive manufacturing sources emphasize process control and post-processing limits, especially aluminum oxidation below ~400 °C.

## Evidence gaps

Most CPO items are company announcements or trade press with no independent measurements or shipping dates. The WAAM review was only partially retrievable. The L-PBF controller was not tested on hardware. The busbar surrogate lacks experimental validation. Several plating and busbar items are vendor or advisory content without measured performance.

topic_weeks.synthesis_md:
## Key developments

All three supplied records are peer-reviewed papers; no patents or news items were provided, so this brief cannot characterize commercial or legal developments.

- **Aluminum MEX feedstock debinding (paper):** For AA6061 feedstocks, the onset oxidation temperature was ~400 °C, so air thermal debinding was kept below that limit. Both solvent-plus-thermal and single-step wick debinding achieved ≥96 wt.% binder removal, but wick-debound samples showed more uniform microstructure and higher sintered density; extending dwell from 2 h to 10 h raised relative density from ~97% to ~98% [Material extrusion-based additive manufacturing of aluminum feedstocks](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40964-026-01995-z).
- **Intralayer L-PBF control (paper):** A data-based predictive FIR proportional controller using coaxial photodiode melt-pool emission signals was evaluated only in closed-loop MATLAB simulation, not on a physical printer. It reported a 99.98% reduction in threshold-exceeding samples in the studied layer and lower RMSE than comparator controllers under tested settings [Design of an intralayer data-based controller for laser powder bed fusion processing](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00170-026-19180-5).
- **WAAM process adaptation (review):** The review positions GMAW, GTAW, and PAW as the metallurgical foundation of WAAM, noting CMT's low heat input and low spatter and the independent wire-feed/arc-power setting of GTAW and PAW; process choice depends on alloy, deposition rate, geometry, and surface quality [Application and Adaptation of Arc-Based Welding Processes to Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing](https://doi.org/10.3390/ma19204362).

## Evidence gaps

Evidence is limited to three papers. The L-PBF controller results are simulation-only and not validated on hardware. The WAAM review's specific data could not be verified because only the abstract and metadata were retrievable. No trend across the field can be established from these records alone.

## Key developments

- **Busbar design guidance (news, advisory):** A buyer guide recommends T2/TU1 oxygen-free copper at typically ≥99.9% IACS, nickel plating of 3–8 µm, and temperature-rise limits such as ≤65 K above ambient, citing contact resistance, hot spots, and thermal-runaway risk as drivers. These are advisory recommendations, not measured results [2026 Energy Storage PACK Busbar Selection Guide](https://www.novaeuris.com/buyer-guide/2026-energy-storage-pack-busbar-selection-guide-co.html).
- **Flexible busbar rationale (news, vendor):** A vendor article argues rigid copper busbars transmit mechanical displacement between mounting points, while flexible sections absorb relative movement between modules, terminals, and supports [EV Busbar Reliability Testing OEM](https://www.stamping-welding.com/info/ev-busbar-environmental-testing-103703886.html).
- **Laser cleaning/welding integration (news, vendor):** A vendor describes a combined laser cleaning and welding gantry for copper EV busbars, addressing oxide contamination and copper's reflectivity, with traceability recording. No measured weld quality or throughput is reported [Integrated Laser Cleaning and Welding System](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/).
- **Zinc anode crystallography (paper, abstract only):** Single-crystal Zn electrodes showed facet-dependent plating and stripping, with repeated cycling redirecting growth to protrusions and dendritic accumulation [Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsenergylett.6c01934).

## Evidence gaps

No patents were supplied. Three of four records are vendor or buyer-guide news without measured performance data; the paper summary is abstract-only. No trend in interconnects can be established from this set.

## Key developments

Co-packaged optics (CPO) dominated this week's records, all of them trade-press or vendor announcements rather than peer-reviewed papers or patents.

- Celestica announced the DS6005, a liquid-cooled ORv3 switch built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 Davisson, claiming up to 102.4 Tbps and 64 x 1.6TbE optically enabled ports with external laser modules [Celestica Introduces the DS6005 Data Center Switch with Co-Packaged Optics to Enable Power-Efficient AI Fabrics](https://news.google.?oc=5). Specifications are preliminary with no sampling or availability dates [Celestica DS6005 Puts 102.4Tbps of Co-Packaged Optics and 64 1.6TbE Ports in a 1.5OU Liquid-Cooled ORv3 Switch](https://news.google.?oc=5).
- Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC demonstrated an integrated optical compute system at OCP, reporting steady eye metrics but no quantitative figures [Wiwynn, Ayar Labs, and GUC Advance Co-Packaged Optics with Live Demonstration of Integrated Optical Compute System at OCP Global Summit 2026](https://news.google.?oc=5).
- Intel claimed sole volume production of InP-on-300mm-silicon and targets below 5 pJ/bit, citing 8 million photonic ICs shipped since 2016 [Intel Makes AI Optical Interconnect Push, Claims to Be Sole Volume Producer of 300mm Indium Phosphide Wafers](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTE13VnE1X0N4SktSZm5GSGpRd1VhSDJaSHEyS3R3M0dfVFcyb29mc1NlclI1aF9SbmE2SzhqZmYwTm84ZmtuZFE2U0xhZXd2YWZrVXpnUjlCS3FtRk5xT3dOSi1tVWRzRlhwTmtUMWRvS1NKaUMzSWc?oc=5).
- Lightmatter and Flex announced 204.8 Tbps CPO for open racks [Lightmatter and Flex Bring 204.8 Tbps Co-Packaged Optics Into Open Racks](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxQbTdFbmozaWdjOGNXeHRxQnloOVRyR2JHdFNaSjBfWlEwN0R0LU5vbTNaWXZGeTFQNmpkRy1aNkZxN3J3TkZMQVFZNFJfTDItMUpDSTdELVRSVjh3cFd5WHZpUl96UHNWZThBY2JlSEY3THVobER1WHhtTnVac3o1NnI3LVdLYXA5bDZRNzdXdkxjNWp1cEtFdFp6aW9kcjFmZmlqUGx0cGxyUQ?oc=5).

## Evidence gaps

No patents or peer-reviewed papers appear in these records. All performance claims are vendor statements without independent measurement, and no commercial adoption or legal status is established. No trend can be confirmed from this sample.

## Key developments
- Han's Laser described an integrated laser cleaning and welding gantry system aimed at copper busbars in EV battery packs, electronic control units, power distribution units, and battery module connections [Integrated Laser Cleaning and Welding System for Automotive Busbars - Han's Laser](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/). This is a vendor news/product description, not a peer-reviewed paper or patent.
- The stated design combines a laser cleaning unit and a laser welding unit on one gantry, with dual left-right workstations, real-time laser distance measurement at each station, and automated welding data recording for traceability [same source](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/).
- The vendor frames the problem as copper surface contamination (oxide layers, oil residues, paint, insulating coatings) plus high thermal conductivity and infrared reflectivity complicating stable weld formation [same source](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/).

## Evidence gaps
- The supplied record contains no measured weld quality, conductivity, throughput, or comparative performance data; the source itself states it does not report these [same source](https://www.hanslaserus.com/knowledge/integrated-laser-cleaning-and-welding-system-for-automotive-busbars/).
- No papers or patents are supplied, and no commercial adoption or legal status is evidenced. With a single vendor record, no trend can be established for aluminum or dissimilar-metal joining specifically.

## Key developments

- STLE has released a free digital special report, *Next-Generation Gear Lubricants for Electric Vehicles*, covering performance demands on EV drivetrain gear lubricants from high-speed, compact gearboxes under demanding loads and elevated temperatures [STLE Releases Report on Next-Generation EV Gear ...](https://jobbersworld.com/2026/10/13/stle-releases-report-on-next-generation-ev-gear-lubricants/).
- The report frames a central trade-off: lower-viscosity fluids can reduce frictional losses and improve drivetrain efficiency, but make it harder to maintain adequate lubricant film strength and wear protection under demanding conditions [STLE Releases Report on Next-Generation EV Gear ...](https://jobbersworld.com/2026/10/13/stle-releases-report-on-next-generation-ev-gear-lubricants/).
- Electrical compatibility and potential effects of stray currents are cited as additional formulation and testing considerations [STLE Releases Report on Next-Generation EV Gear ...](https://jobbersworld.com/2026/10/13/stle-releases-report-on-next-generation-ev-gear-lubricants/).

This is a single news item reporting on a trade-body report; no patents or peer-reviewed papers are supplied.

## Evidence gaps

- The item supplies no measured data, test results, or comparisons to prior art, so no performance claims can be verified [STLE Releases Report on Next-Generation EV Gear ...](https://jobbersworld.com/2026/10/13/stle-releases-report-on-next-generation-ev-gear-lubricants/).
- With only one source, no trend can be established, and no commercial adoption or legal status is evidenced.
- The underlying STLE report itself is not among the supplied records.

## Key developments

- **Electroless nickel bath chemistry (trade article, originally 1994):** In a lactate-acetate EN bath at 87°C/pH 4.6, the lithium bath gave the fastest initial rate (19 µm/h vs 13 µm/h for sodium), but precipitated after a few turnovers; the ammonium bath was slowest yet the only one to reach six MTO without precipitation, attributed to ammonia's nickel complexing. Hot filtration of lithium phosphite reportedly raised rate from 16.3 to 17.5 µm/h in a 1.75-MTO bath [The Effect of Monovalent Cations on Electroless Nickel Plating](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3049-the-effect-of-monovalent-cations-on-electroless-nickel-plating).
- **Zinc anode plating (paper, abstract only):** Single-crystal Zn electrodes showed facet-dependent deposition morphologies on (002), (100), and (101); stripping left geometry-defined pits that were not preferentially refilled, and repeated cycling redirected growth to protrusions and mossy/dendritic accumulation [Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsenergylett.6c01934).
- **Hybrid EDM electrodes (review):** Printed ABS cores with electroless plus electrolytic copper coatings gave comparable material removal rate, wear, and surface roughness to solid copper in most comparative studies, but were inferior in several and wore 1.1–2.8 times faster; copper shell service-life data are lacking [Hybrid tool electrodes for EDM](https://doi.org/10.15826/chimtech.10451).
- **Industry news:** JIT Industries acquired Birmingham-based Precision Plating, an industrial hard chrome facility; no financial terms or capacity figures disclosed [JIT Industries Acquires Birmingham-Based Chrome Plating Facility](https://finishingandcoating.com/index.php/plating/3056-jit-industries-acquires-birmingham-based-chrome-plating-facility).

- The EN article is a 1994 reprint; the Zn paper was assessed from abstract only. No trend across records can be established.

## Key developments

Co-packaged optics (CPO) dominated this week's thermal-relevant news, with several vendor announcements at OCP Global Summit 2026. Celestica introduced the DS6005, a fully liquid-cooled ORv3 switch built on Broadcom's Tomahawk 6 – Davisson, described as delivering up to 102.4 Tbps with 64 1.6TbE ports and external laser modules [Celestica Unveils DS6005 Co-Packaged Optics Switch for AI Data Centers - Unite.AI](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilwFBVV95cUxOMzk2OERwakJjRnhHT1ZqM3BVSHd6MmlhT0wwWkNyWUxOYUduaC1yRTJ5RkVfbmRCa0NmdXNNdjh5Z1NmcmVHWUdzZXZfVk12aGlJOUxjZ0p4TDdYTUNPcXQza2lvUUVfY3lhNmJpNEIzd25CSTZqTzZoVVlwcU5NRGdXaEVFdVhoLWxwWUN1V0F4aXRwRldR?oc=5). StorageReview adds that specifications are preliminary, with no sampling or availability dates and no published power or latency figures [Celestica DS6005 Puts 102.4Tbps of Co-Packaged Optics and 64 1.6TbE Ports in a 1.5OU Liquid-Cooled ORv3 Switch - StorageReview.com](https://news.google.?oc=5).

Separately, Wiwynn, Ayar Labs and GUC reported a live OCP demonstration integrating optical engines in multi-chip packages, with telemetry tracking thermal and wavelength drift [Wiwynn, Ayar Labs, and GUC Advance Co-Packaged Optics with Live Demonstration of Integrated Optical Compute System at OCP Global Summit 2026 - PR Newswire](https://news.google.?oc=5).

On the research side, a Frontiers paper presented a simulation-trained surrogate for thermal-risk assessment of bolted busbar joints, reporting XGBoost R² = 0.990 ± 0.005, while noting the framework is geometry-specific and not experimentally validated [Interpretable surrogate modeling for load-aware thermal risk assessment of bolted switchgear busbar joints using electro-thermal simulation](https://doi.org/10.3389/fmech.2026.1904437).

## Evidence gaps

All CPO items are vendor announcements or trade coverage, not independent measurements; no verified power, latency or reliability data were supplied. No patents appeared in the records. The busbar buyer guides are advisory, not experimental [2026 Energy Storage PACK Busbar Selection Guide: Conductive Copper Components for Battery Packs-NovaEuris](https://www.novaeuris.com/buyer-guide/2026-energy-storage-pack-busbar-selection-guide-co.html).
